narrative_x: I am a resident of [NAME] in Allston. Over the past few months, there has been quite a bit of construction on my street. Specifically, the block of [NAME] on which I live has been closed to traffic. There are no detour signs, or other warnings as I approach that I will need to find an alternate path. In trying to ask a question about which streets WERE open to residents, I was treated as a nuisance, and my questions idioc. I was raised to believe that P.O.s are helpful, civic‐minded people, who are interested in helping the public. Furthermore, I teach children that they should feel comfortable asking for assistance from an officer‐ I now understand why many of them do not. I realize that directing traffic on a cold day is an unpleasant task. It does not have to be made more unpleasant by disrespect and condescension. If your officers are not prepared to assist residents as they attempt to access their homes, please make sure that detour signs are posted so that we are aware of where we CAN go. I also realize that, compared with the other more serious issues of keeping a large city safe, this seems very trivial. But as a taxplayer, and as a human being, I don''t feel that I should be treated in this manner.

narrative_x: On July fourth at approximately 1pm, I was riding my bicycle a few bike lengths behind my friend as we were heading from the North End on Atlantic Avenue. We were both riding in the designated bike lane as we turned left with traffic onto the Surface road. As we were approaching the red light at the pedestrian crossing from Faneuil Hall to the greenway, a motorcycle that was traveling in the lane next to me, cut me off to get into the bike lane (and I assume dash around the stopped cars). I nearly was knocked off my bike and into the curb. My friend and I noticed a uniformed P.O. sitting in his car right next to us and we motioned for him to do something about the motorcycle driving dangerously. When the officer emerged from his vehicle and I was gesturing at the motorcycle, he clearly was upset at being bothered and was quite belligerent, even after seeing how upset and angry I was. We tried to tell him what happened and he started to yell at me for "tailgating" the motorcycle. The detective did not want to listen to what we were trying to say, and just became angrier...telling us how we disturbed his 5 minute break from the miserable heat. How he had to wear his uniform and work on the fourth July only to have us yell at him. To be fair, I was angry, not at the detective (at first) but at nearly being run off the road. But when he started blaming *me* saying it was my fault, I did get angry at the officer. Perhaps he did not see what happened in front of him from inside his car, but his rapid jump to a false conclusion that the cyclist is always wrong is extremely disheartening. Same Road, Same Rules. I was in the bike lane, signaled my turn and stopped at the red light but was yelled at for "tailgating" a motorcycle that cut me off to drive into the bike lane. In the end, we all shook hands and went our own way, but looking back at the situation there are a few concerns. First and foremost is that P.O.s should know the rules of the road. Boston is making a push to be a bike‐friendly city but, when in any situation, the assumption is that the cyclist is at fault and risks verbal abuse and insults when appealing for help, it is extremely disheartening. Second, the detective should have assessed the situation and seen that I was upset by what happened on the road. It was extremely unprofessional of his to become belligerent and escalate the situation. I am sure the BPD would not appreciate the large crowd that gathered at the crosswalk to witness his vitriol. Finally, the department may want to reconsider placing detectives who may not regularly interact with masses of the public in such a busy location on a major holiday. I appreciate that so many officers have to give up their holiday so we can enjoy ours, but do you really want the face of the BPD to tourists and visitors to be that of an angry officer “put out” by his temporary assignment? Thank you, [NAME]

narrative_x: A P.O. walked to his car which was parked right outside the South St exit at Forest Hills. A gentleman was standing about 5 feet from the doors when the officer got into his car, with windows rolled up and proceeded to drive...The man standing near the door, it seems was in the officers way. The man standing there stared at the car, and then the office hit his horn. The man did not move and I could see he was puzzled about the officers behavior. Was he honking at him? For what reason? So the officer pulls up to him, finally rolls his window down and they talk. (I could not hear what was said) HOWEVER, I did hear the officer in a rather rude and tense tone told the man "Are you telling me where I can and cannot drive and what I can and cannot not do?" The gentleman responded "No" and the officer became even more tense and aggressive and stated "Next time I will just run over you." I was speechless. The man standing there had no idea what the officer was doing or what direction he was taking. He was never rude to the officer and in fact, the officer could have introduced himself and told him he was in his way and if he could please move. I wonder now, why people complain about officers at Forest Hills being rude to them. I stood there watching the entire incident wondering what happened to "Good afternoon sir, could you move out of the way?" That is all the officer had to say. And like I mentioned, he never introduced himself. No need to be rude and nasty. I do not have any information about who he is as I did not want to confront him. The officer was tall, about 45...maybe older? When the officer drove away I asked the gentleman what had happened and he said "The cop was a jerk. I stood here not knowing why he was hitting his horn and he was a typical rude cop." I don't think they are all bad people, like any profession a police man can have a bad day or he could do his without being super friendly but there is no excuse for that degree of rudeness. I'm sure the BPD has many more pressing maers to deal with but gaining the publics trust is VERY important in my eyes.

My brother is a P.O. and I am well aware of the things they have to put up with so I make sure to pay due respect which is why I was quite shocked at how unprofessional and rude this officer was to me. I would never use profanities when speaking to an officer and would never expect them to use profanities when speaking to me. It was completely uncalled for especially given the fact that there was no reduced speed sign (which the officer admitted), I did not refuse to follow any directions, nor did I display any rude or threatening behavior. I realize this may not seem to be a serious complaint, but I feel that this sort of behavior reflects poorly on the profession as a whole and is part of the reason many officers are, in fact, treated with disrespect. I do hope this maer is addressed. Thank you.

I find this extremely unsettling and troublesome. Because of this crime I have had to spend thousands of mine own dollars. I have had to take time away from my graduate program and work. narrative_x: This took place at the Red Sox World Series game 6 inside the park. I had tickets to the game and went down to Yawkey Way around the 6th inning to go to the smoking section. As I was walking back to my section, while still on Yawkey Way, there was a gate that blocked the public off at the South side of Yawkey, with a large crowd against it anticipating the win. I ran by and yelled "Go Sox!", as I had seen a couple other people do. The crowd cheered and I trotter to the stairs to head to my section. However I was quickly grabbed by 3 Fenway security guards who said "nice try buddy". They told me that a P.O. saw me jump the fence. Even after producing my ticket, they still wouldn't budge. When they took me to the officer upon request, he told me flat out he watched me jump the fence, not to bullshit him, told me to get out and directed the security guards to push me out. I tried to ask him specifics on where on the fence he saw me climb and jump, and was very tame and respectable (I had not even been drinking), however Officer Panchovich would not listen. Standing outside the gate, ticket in hand (a ticket that cost $1600), trembling, I called my mother who was at our seats. At about that time, about 60 seconds after I was kicked out, Officer Panchovich yelled at me from inside the gate and said "You! Are you the one we just kicked out?" I responded yes, and he came outside and grabbed me by the arm and pulled me inside (not with force or anything that hurt, but still disrespectful and unnecessary contact). He asked me if I jumped the fence, and once again I said no and produced my ticket. AT THIS POINT‐‐‐Everything could have been a misunderstanding‐‐Officer Panchovich could have said I thought you jumped because when I turned and looked it seemed that way, or could have apologized for lying, or could have said listen it is a big game, things are tight around here, I can't risk anything. INSTEAD, after he asked what I did and I explained how I yelled go sox to the crowd, Officer Panchovich accused me of trying to incite a riot. This is frankly absurd and an abuse of authority that I believe is common in police departments (not necessarily BPD, I have had very good encounters and experiences with you all). Officer Panchovich did this purely for selfish reasons‐‐ 1) so he would not have to admit he lied, 2) he could further reassert his authority, 3) so if I wanted to discuss it further or accuse/ask him why he lied, he would have a reason to throw me out again, or worse, arrest me. This is the kind of attitude that is detrimental to the police today. I completely understand that given the recent events in Boston, and the magnitude of the event, that security was tighter and the stakes were higher. But no one says being a P.O. is an easy job. Things were quiet on Yawkey Way at that point, most people were in the park watching the game. If Officer Panchovich had just admitted he lied, at the least (discussing and hearing me out the first time before I was kicked out would have been nice) said listen I'm sorry but I can't deal with this right now, it would not have been an issue. If I was in Officer Panchovich's shoes, I would have stopped me too, if I had turned around when the crowd cheered. I probably would have asked what I just did and if I had a ticket. That would be the right way to handle things. But even if I didn't do that, the right thing to do is admit your wrong doing, apologize, or just say go on your way, NOT try to make up a crime so you do not have to deal with your mistake. All I want is Officer Panchovich to realize there is no shame in admitting you were wrong, or apologizing to a citizen you falsely accused. It takes a mature adult to do that. And can be tough, I am sure tougher in a position of authority. But being a cop is a hard job. If Officer Panchovich wants to write an apology, that is his choice, but I do want to know that he read this report, whether he agrees, disagrees, thinks I am crazy or doesn't care, I just want him to read it. Please contact me at [EMAIL] with a response. Thanks again. (Sent via bpdnews.com)

narrative_x: I have never complained about a P.O.. I have the upmost respect for the people that I use to work with. But today, I am fed up with one particular officer and the way he treats people. On March 5, 2016, I was driving midway down on Truman Pkwy. Officer #3361 was in the middle of the road pulling over a car in front of me. I went into the left lane and he said I needed to pull over, too. I asked him why I was pulled over. He asked for my license and registration and then said I went over 51mph. There was no equipment on him to indicate what my speed was. I know I was going at 45mph, but not over that. I travel that area all time and know that bicyclists and pedestrians usually are in the area and to be careful. Two weeks prior to that, I saw a dog get hit by a car near Commonwealth Ave and was shaken up about it. Therefore, I don't go over more than 5 miles of the speed limit. And over there, the speed limit is 40mph. I called the Hyde Park Police Dept. and spoke to the supervisor on duty. He informed me that I could ask the officer how he knew my speed. I informed the supervisor that this officer is well‐known in the community as an officer that likes to give tickets and that he is very disrespectful and rude. I told the supervisor I would ask. When the Officer #3361 came back, he told me, "I don't have to answer to you!" He said that I needed to follow the instructions on the back of the cket and appeal it. I informed him that his supervisor said that I was allowed to ask him the queson of how he gave me the cket. "I don't have to talk to you!" After receiving the ticket, I went to the station to make a complaint. I informed the supervisor that I know that people speed on Truman Parkway, but that's usually around after midnight when they know that P.O.s are not in the area. I live in the neighborhood and notice everything that changes. I've called the police when crimes are being commied in or around my neighborhood. I have dealt with P.O.s before as a social worker, as a volunteer for high profiled events, and in the non‐profit sector. I have never in my life met a rude and obnoxious P.O. that disrespects individuals when he is talking to them. It is my right to know why the officer pulled me over as well as my right to know how he came to that conclusion. But when an officer yells at you and feels that he is above the law and above you...well, this is not acceptable. I have made my complaint known to the Hyde Park Police Dept about my observations since this is the second time I have dealt with Officer #3361. I am also very aware that there are many people in the community who know this Officer and the type the work he does. Each person has had the same complaint. If the community is to respect P.O.s, shouldn't P.O.s offer respect to the community? I'm very distraught by dealing with this officer. Frankly, I thought he moved to another location where he is more needed or change his hours to deal with traffic safety in the middle of the night when it really is a time when speeding occurs in the area.

narrative_x: I am truly appalled with the way our emergency phone call was handled last evening. Around 10:15 last evening my roommate and I were disrupted by someone ringing our buzzer for approximately 15‐minutes straight. When the buzzing finally stopped, we heard someone in our hallway speaking in hushed tone in a different language (there are no foreigners in our building so this extremely alarming). The next thing we know the person is outside our door banging and trying to break in, turning the door knob and trying to get it open. My roommate and I immediately went downstairs and called 911. This was around 10:35/10:45 or so. In our 911 call we stated that someone was trying to break into our apartment. We did not see an officer until approximately 11:30pm after we had to call THREE TIMES. I recommend you listen to the 911 call because the Dispatcher was incredibly rude with my roommate and I found that to be completely unprofessional. When the officers finally arrived they didn't even get out of the cruiser and come into the apartment. We had to leave our apartment (bear in mind we don't have a peep hole so we had no idea if the person was in our building still or not), and go talk to the officers on the street while they sat in their cruiser. While speaking to them they told us that they had already been to our building and searched and say nothing. This was a complete lie. Our apartment is on the first floor and is maybe 30 feet from the main entrance to the building. We were sitting near our door the entire time and would have heard if the officers came in. Not only that, they said they buzzed random units in the building and were let in. Again, also a lie. if someone had been buzzed in we 100% would have heard it because we're so close to the door. The officer proceeded to tell us that it was nothing to worry about ‐ it was probably just their "DK" friend who hangs out on the wall outside of the Bank of America parking lot across from [NAME] on West Broadway because they saw him walking down the street drunk earlier. Regardless of who they speculate it to be, there is no reason for them to not come inside our apartment and provide us with the feeling of safety we were desperately after. I had to beg the officers to please come in and check the basement portion of our building because it would have been very easy to someone to go down there and go unnoticed and I did not feel safe going back to sleep until they confirmed the building was safe. The very nature of the entire interaction was unprofessional and did not leave up the "protect and serve" that I would expect to come from officers. I have never had a negative opinion of P.O.s and in a world where there are so many people who do, I really would have thought the officers who responded would have showed more care and concern. My opinion is severely altered after last evening. The fact that we were so blatantly lied to and that it took over an hour for someone to respond to our call is really upsetting and frustrating. What if the situation were more severe? What if the outcome wasn't what it was? There are so many variables at play in a world as scary as ours is today and I wish the officers had done more to make us feel safe, because to be perfectly honest I did not feel safe in my home last night, largely due to their lack of concern for us.

narrative_x: I was cycling home from work and had just rounded the corner from Court Street to Cambridge Street. I was riding as far to the right as possible when a silver 4 door sedan (older model car) passed very close to me. I gestured with a "what the heck" motion to indicate that they were too close. The individual in the passenger seat gave me the middle finger out the window. I caught up to the car as it stopped in the turn lane at a red light at the intersection of Sudbury and Cambridge Streets and pulled up to the driver's side window. I was shocked to see two P.O.s in the car. They were not in uniform, but had badges around their necks. I offered my hand to the officer at the wheel and introduced myself. I asked why they passed so close and then gave me the middle finger. The officers denied doing anything wrong and immediately became very defensive. They claim they gave me plenty of space and that I could not expect to take up the whole road. Last time I checked, bikes ARE allowed to take a lane if necessary, but as noted above, I was very far to the right. If they truly had not done anything wrong, why did they give me the finger? I was angry and my adrenaline was pumping (as it does when you are almost hit by a car) but at no time was I threatening to the officers, myself or anyone around me. So you can imagine my surprise when the officers pulled forward to block two lanes of traffic (for no apparent reason other than to make a scene), got out of the car, twisted my arm behind my back pushing me against the back of the car and threatened to arrest me! When I voiced my surprise at being physically accosted, one of the officers said something about striking an officer. This is an exaggeration equivalent to me saying that they broke my arm when they twisted it behind my back. I find it very difficult believe that they were threatened by a 5'6" 135# female straddling a bike. Instead, it appears their reaction was an attempt to inmidate someone who confronted them for their mistakes. The reason for my complaint is not only to make someone aware of this incident, but also to voice my disappointment. As an eight year military veteran ( Army Officer 2005‐2013), I have always held uniformed individuals in the highest regard, believing that while the occasional bad egg exists in all services, most were good people who did the right thing. This incident destroyed that belief and trust. These officers endangered my life, disrespected me with that hand gesture, used unnecessary physical force, blatantly lied, and threatened me with arrest for voicing concerns over their actions. My family, friends and coworkers have asked why I did not get a picture of the officers or their license plate, but in that moment I was afraid to reach for my backpack to get my phone for fear that these officers would see is as a threatening movement and escalate the situation further. I never thought I would have to be fearful around P.O.s (especially having done nothing wrong), and now I'm saddened to say that I not only fear and mistrust them, but do not feel like they are concerned about my or any other cyclists' safety.

narrative_x: I called 911 to report a man trying to break into my house. I indicated to the dispatcher that I was home alone and a man was trespassing in my back yard trying to break the glass pane on my backdoor. I gave a description of the man and all of my contact information. The 911 dispatcher stayed on the phone with me until I saw a police cruiser at which time she told me they would handle it from there. However, the officers NEVER came to my house. They were 2 doors down where they found the man who had attempted to break into my house. As I was approaching the officers they were hurriedly putting the man in the unmarked cruiser and were about to leave WITHOUT ever checking in with me to see if I was ok or if the man had caused any damage to my property. When I did manage to stop one of the officer to inquire about what was happening he was totally dismissive. There was no report taken on the incident and I was not given any information other than "he's just drunk and thought it was his house". Last I checked trespassing on private property is against the law. For the officers to not even bother to check in on me, the victim of a crime, or at the very least inquire about any property damage is very disheartening. I am a home owner and I have been an active member of this neighborhood as the president of the board at Madison Park Development Corp, a board member at DSNI as well as commissioner of the Red Sox Foundation's softball league. I have always advocated for a better relationship between my community and the BPD. To have officers in my community, in my district be so utterly dismissive after what was a terrifying event is really discouraging.

narrative_x: While conducting an investigation at my workplace with several other detectives, I overheard Sgt. O'Neill make two troubling comments to her colleagues. I did not engage with her in the moment because the investigation she was part of was urgent, and it would have been disrespectful of the work to pull her away to address her comments. I was also on the clock and obligated to focus on my work. While observing that people often fail to contact the police in a timely manner to report crimes, she said that "even with domestic violence, these kids will call their sister or mother first before us". Prior to that, she had been complaining about the ways that civilians report crime, and her overall tone in the conversation was dismissive and unprofessional. As a victim of domestic violence myself, I have had great difficulty in requesting and receiving police assistance. Victims of violence experience shock, dissociation, and memory loss, which can prevent them from calling in the crime. These and other symptoms of trauma need to be considered by responding officers. Sadly, in my experience responding officers are untrained in handling domestic violence and respond with incompetence. This lack of training is of course not their fault, but it leads to ineffective handling of the crime, and sometimes insulting and dismissive treatment of the victim. This often deters victims from seeking future help when they are re‐victimized, which is statistically likely. The poor treatment I received from responding officers was a direct factor in my decision to not seek police assistance when I experienced violence in the future. Sgt. O'Neill's comments were inappropriate because she demonstrated an ignorance of structural barriers that make it difficult for victims to request and receive police support. This is troubling to observe in a P.O.. Additionally, she said that "cyclists are killing us all" by "always running stop signs and red lights". This is an inaccurate stereotype, and again troubling to see in a P.O.. Most traffic violations are committed by motorists, and cyclists. Most accidents between cyclists and motorists are fatal or injurious to cyclists, not drivers. Police in Boston fail to hold drivers accountable in these accidents, even those who operate in unsafe and illegal manners. Every cyclist I know in this city has been injured by a car, most of them seriously. To deny these citizens protection on the road because of ignorance and misinformation is absurd, and frankly unacceptable.

At the entrance of the whole foods parking lot, there is often a lot of back up on a monday night due to the substantial number of individuals doing their shopping. I was turning left into the entrance of the parking lot, requiring me to cross two lanes of traffic. There was a long line of cars in the farthest of the two lanes, all waiting to turn right into the entrance of the parking lot, and then the lane closest to me was empty. The person who's turn it was to turn right into the parking lot waved for me to go when the cars started moving, so I went but there were a lot of pedestrians crossing so i couldn't go into the lot quite yet. Then the person behind me followed me and blocked the two lanes of traffic. We were stuck like this for about one full minute when two P.O.s stopped their car in the middle of the two lanes (the one without all the other cars turning right into the parking lot) and one of them came up to my window, though i now could've continued forward into the parking lot, and banged his flashlight on my window. The other cop did the same to the car behind me. I put my window down and he started yelling at me "what do you think you're doing? are you an idiot? you're completely blocking the intersection" i apologized and he asked for my license and registration. I gave him my license and he continued to yell at me asking "what do you think you're doing? are you an idiot? this is an infraction i'm going to fine you" and i continued to apologize. I understand that I was in the wrong and the cop could've given me a ticket, so i appreciated it when he did drop it and let me go. However, I was apologetic and calm the whole time and did not disagree with him, so in the future i think it's fair to ask your officers to not persistently yell at calm, complacent individuals and call me them an idiot, and instead explain to them what to do differently next time. Because now i'm not even sure what i should've done differently and would love to know. I don't want to hate P.O.s, and I know they're just trying to do their jobs/get people to do what they are supposed to be doing, but I would appreciate it if they knew when not to yell at people who apologize and want to learn from their mistake. I apologized for the misunderstanding but the Officer continued to berate me and finally told me to pull over until he was ready to let me into the entrance to the hotel. I felt as though the Officer was taunng me to argue with him, which I did not. I know beer than that. I did not want to file this complaint, but I feel that the department should know about this. I am 56 years old and have lived here for 36 years. Never before have I felt such intimidation. I know that area is crazy with congestion, but I did not do anything to warrant this kind of behavior. I did feel lucky that I was not a person of color or female, I do not know what the Officer may have reacted. That is how inmidated I felt. In the photograph, Detective McManus can be seen wearing pants that have a wide reflective stripe along the side as well as brown shoes with a white sole. Captain Fong instructed me to inform Detective McManus of this infraction, ascertain his explanation and to reprimand him verbally. Detective McManus seemed embarrassed and contrite in his explanation. Detective McManus explained that he wore the reflective striped pants as an extra measure for visibility. Detective McManus explained that his function at this particular site is to halt traffic on Purchase Street and pull traffic from the parking garage as well as preventing back up and gridlock. Detective McManus further explained that when he left his house in the morning, he forgot his regulation black colored uniform shoes and only had the brown colored shoes he had worn earlier in the day. narrative_x: About 10:38pm on Wednesday 06/17/2020, Officer Beggan assigned to the F441F responded to a radio call for a Assault and Battery in Progress at the intersection of Hardy Street and East 8th Street, Boston. ¶ Assisting units on scene were the F411F (Brian Fitzgerald) and F431F(Arthur Fritch). ¶ Upon arrival, officers observed two males standing outside of 2 Hardy Street on the sidewalk. Officers also observed two females and a male on the sidewalk in front of 1 Hardy Street. ¶ Officers approached the two females and a male outside of 1 Hardy Street due to one of the females visibly upset sitting on the curb. Officer Beggan spoke with the reporting party, Mr. Brady DeAngelo, who stated he and his two friends arrived in the area of Hardy Street looking for a lost cell phone. Mr. DeAngelo stated they eventually were able to ping the location of the missing phone to the area of 2 Hardy Street. Mr. DeAngelo stated he and his two friends were continuously walking the premise around 2 Hardy Street then attempted to make contact with the residents. Mr. DeAngelo stated his two female friends began ringing the door bell and knocking on the front door. ¶ Officers then spoke to Ms. Alexis Aggouras, who was visibly upset while sitting on the sidewalk opposite 2 Hardy Street. When asked what had happened, Ms. Aggouras stated she lost her phone after spending the day at the beach and eventually pinged its location to the area of Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she and her two friends were looking under vehicles, in the street, and around the premise of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she believed her phone could possibly be inside the residence of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she repeatedly rang the doorbell and knocked several times on the front door in an attempt to make contact with the residents. After ringing and knocking on the door, an unknown male exited the front door of the residence and grabbed her and her friend in neck area. At this moment, the male began forcing Ms. Aggouras and her friend off of the stairs at 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras denied EMS on scene and stated she did not suffer any injuries.  While speaking with Ms. Aggouras, officers could smell a strong scent consistent with the smell of an alcohol beverage mixture emanating from her breathe. ¶ Officers spoke with Ms. Elise Rosen, who stated she was accompanying Ms. Aggouras at the front door of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Rosen stated she and Ms. Aggouras attempted to locate Ms. Aggouras' phone by attempting to get in contact with the residents of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Rosen stated she and Ms. Aggouras began ringing the door bell and knocking on the front door. Ms. Rosen stated after knocking on the door and ringing the bell, a male eventually exited 2 Hardy Street and physically grabbed her and Ms. Aggouras in the neck area. Ms. Rosen stated the male physically pushed her and Ms. Aggouras off of the front stairs, yelling in their faces. Ms. Rosen stated she, Ms. Aggouras, and Mr. DeAngelo separated from the unknown male and notified police. Ms. Rosen informed officers she and Ms. Aggouras spent a day at the beach and admitted to consuming alcohol throughout the day. ¶ Officers spoke to Mr. Daniel Fitzgerald, who stated he was suddenly woken up when he heard his doorbell being continually rung. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he then heard excessively loud banging, consistent with the noise of trying to gain access into a locked door. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was unsure if someone was trying to break in. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he got dressed and quickly ran down to his front door to confront the excessive banging. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he opened his front door, in the darkness, and observed three unknown parties on the front porch of his property aggressively demanding for a cell phone.  The three parties began to yell, shout, and accuse him of stealing a phone while stepping closer towards the front door of Mr. Fitzgerald's residence. At this moment, Mr. Fitzgerald grabbed two parties, independently and attempted to escort them off of the property. Mr. Fitzgerald relayed that he verbally demanded the parties to get off his property as they continued to accuse him for stealing a cell phone. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was able to escort the parties on to the public sidewalk outside of his residence. Mr. Fitzgerald stated the two females involved in the altercation were intoxicated and acting hysterically. Mr. Fitzgerald informed officers that the three parties stated they were calling police to which Mr. Fitzgerald responded "please do." Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was unaware of the situation regarding a lost phone and was concerned as to why three unknown parties were at his front door aggressively shouting and making false accusations. ¶ Officers spoke with Ms. Rosen a second time who stated a neighbor, who resides on the first floor apartment of 2 Hardy Street, stated he located a bag on his front steps. The neighbor, later identified as Mr. Lawrence Norton, stated to Ms. Rosen he located a cell phone in the bag but it was out of battery power. In order to attempt to locate the owner, Mr. Norton began charging the phone. While the phone was charging, Mr. Norton heard a loud commotion outside of his home and exited his residence. Mr. Norton eventually learned he was in possession of the lost phone, and was able to return it to Ms. Aggouras. Officers spoke with both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen who stated the phone was returned along with the bag it was left in. Both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen confirmed nothing from the bag was missing. Ms. Rosen also confirmed the phone was possibly dead or shut off due to not being able to ping the location of the phone right away. ¶ Speaking with Ms. Aggouras, Ms. Rosen, and Mr. DeAngelo officers offered to request Boston EMS on scene for a medical evaluation to which both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen denied repeatedly. Officers asked the parties where they would be staying for the night to which they replied Ms. Rosen's residence in Dorchester. Concerned with both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen being under the influence due to her own omission, officers offered to drive the parties home. Mr. DeAngelo informed officers he had his motor vehicle on scene. Mr. DeAngelo did not appear to be under the influence of alcohol and was in a safe condition to operate a motor vehicle. Prior to leaving the scene, Ms. Aggouras was visibly upset and stated "I'm sorry" several times to which officers informed her she had nothing to apologize for. Mr. DeAngelo and Ms. Rosen stated they were thankful for the officers on scene and proceeded to return back to Ms. Rosen's residence. ¶ It should be known there was an unidentified male on scene who did not wish to answer any questions. The unidentified male was a white male, about nineteen to twenty-two years of age, with curly dark hair, and a green shirt. ¶ I was notified of the incident after the officers had returned to the station.  Officer Brian Fitzgerald told me that Daniel Fitzgerald is his uncle and is also a Boston Police officer, currently assigned to the SORI unit. While the call was ongoing, I was checking the Netviewer system and had actually called Officer Brian Fitzgerald to channel 7 and requested him to call the DS line at 617-343-4737.  I asked if they were all set on the call (ie locating victim) and I was advised that they were almost done.  At no time did Officer Fitzgerald notify me that the incident was an alleged assault and battery involving his uncle (family) nor a police officer.  He told me when he got back to the station, well after the complainants had left the area.  He also did not have his Bodycam operating while he was attending to the incident. ¶ At no time did off-duty Daniel Fitzgerald ask for a Patrol Supervisor to respond to the scene as well. ¶ Officer Arthur Fritz responded to assist Officer Brian Fitzgerald and Officer Matt Beggan during the incident. narrative_x: On January 23, 2009 I worked the 330-1130 shift in full uniform assigned as system wide coverage for the Explosive Detection Unit in an unmarked Ford Expedition with MBTA Police Plate 121. At Approx. 10:25 pm I was traveling in the left hand lane of Rt 3 Southbound between exits 15 & 14 in light traffic. Suddenly I noticed headlights behind me . This car got to within 3-4 feet of my rear bumper, so close I lost sight of its headlights. Before I could it react, this car ¶ began to pass me on the right. I immediately activated the blue lights as the car came along side me. I could see the reflection of the blue lights on this car as it cut back into the left lane coming so close to my front end. I had to apply the brakes to prevent this car from striking me. The car just kept going. I observed this car to be a Chevrolet Impala bearing Ma reg 73EL67. Coming up behind with lights still activated the car made no attempt to stop for approximately the next ½ mile. Finally the car pulled into the right lane, slowed and appeared to be stopping only to speed up and continue on. I activated the siren now without any response. The Impala got off at exit 14 rt 228, came to the bottom of the ramp and stopped at the red light. I pulled the cruiser to the left of this car and angled it infront of this car partially blocking its path. No sooner did I exit the cruiser to approach, the car sped off through the intersection. It pulled into the Home Depot Parking lot and turned around coming at me on my left. I stopped short of the car, exited and confronted the operator and only occupant; the drivers window now down. I demanded his license and registration. He yelled in response who are you? I replied, "the police" and again demanded his paperwork. What police? he argued. The Transit Police I replied. I asked a third time for his license and registration and informed him he would be subject to arrest if he did not comply. With this the operator put the car in drive and began to slowly pull away. I reached in grabbed his left hand and pulled his arm out of the window. I now had the subject in a wrist lock and at the same time order him to place the car in park. He told me I was in trouble now and to keep it up and "do what you have to do" as he would sue me civillialy. It wasn't until I applied pressure on the wrist lock as a pain compliance technique did the subject put the car in park. Asked for his license and registration again he yelled "where are we now" in apparent reference to my jurisdiction. I physically took him out of the car with the wrist lock and as I was cuffing him, a Boston Police cavalierly badge fell from his vest pocket. Asked if he was a police officer he responded, "Keep it up kid. Do what you have to do I'll sue you." A pat frisk revealed no weapons on him. I retrieved a Ma. license and Boston Police Id card from his right front pocket identifying him as Detective Robert Tully of Hanover, Ma. I inquired about weapons and he stated his department Glock was in the bag. After turning the ignition off and removing the keys, I checked the compartment area for weapons. I seated Mr. Tully in the passenger seat out of the elements. His department firearm was located in the trunk which I kept for safe keeping. I then removed the handcuffs and had Mr. Tully wait in his car. While conversing with Mr. Tully I now detected an aroma of alcohol on his breath. I notified duty supervisor, Sgt. Cantella of the situation and requested a supervisor from our agency as well as Boston Police to take charge of Mr. Tully, his department cruiser and firearm. Sgt. Roy responded to assist. Sgt Cantella informed me that Lt. Lanchester of C-11 was apprised of the situation. BPD. Officers Giannetti, Fogerty and Sgt. Brennan all from C-11 responded. During this time, Mr. Tully apparently could not wait had to take a bathroom break before this encounter was over. I issued Mr. Tully two citations #'s M1803359 & M1803360 for following too closely, passing on the right, reckless operation and refusal to submit, both criminal complaints issued in hand. Mr. Tully, his weapon and cruiser were turned over to Sgt. Brennan before Sgt. I believe the behavior -- both the masking and refusal to provide the badge number, to be in violation of the Governor's order, the department's own requirement, city COVID requirements and professional standards.

Mr. Robert Toney stated the following:    On March 5, 2021, between 6:30 a.m.- 7:00 a.m., he met his girlfriend at the Liberty Diner, located at 1003 Mass Avenue. He stated that they observed two Boston Police Officers (not in uniform) sitting having breakfast when they walked in. He noted that he knew they were officers by their radios and their badges. ¶ He described that he and his girlfriend also sat down at a table to have breakfast. He described that his girlfriend got up to use the restroom. At this point, the black officer made a sound and then proceeded to tell the white officer, "Look at that ass". He turned around and verbally confronted the officer. The officer, in turn, continued to apologize for the comment that was made. ¶ Mr. Toney stated the black officer appeared to be nervous or embarrassed about the situation and left quickly. However, the white officer still had not paid his bill and stayed a little longer to pay. Mr. Toney provided MA Reg #4ES695 (red Mazda) as the white officer's vehicle. He noted that he did not get a chance to get the vehicle from the officer who commented. ¶ Additionally, Mr. Toney stated that the white officer did not do anything wrong but look toward his girlfriend. However, he felt that the black officer was very disrespectful by making such a comment. He described the officer as a blk male, 230lbs, 5'9" with glasses.

On June 2, 2021, Jose Morales called IAD and spoke with the on-call investigator.  Morales stated that he drives a delivery truck and earlier that day, he was making a delivery of produce to Honeygrow at 100 Northern Avenue, Boston.  Morales stated that there is a construction site in front of that address and he asked a construction worker if he could park there for a few minutes while he made his delivery.  Morales alleged that the construction worker granted him permission, but a police officer who was working the detail told him to move his truck.  Morales and the officer exchanged words during which the officer allegedly shoved Morales with both hands, forcing Morales backward into a parked vehicle.  Morales denied doing anything that would warrant such an act.  Morales took a photograph of the officer's badge which is #561.  The badge is issued to Sgt. Det. Keith Webb.  Webb was assigned to McCourt Construction detail on this date.  Morales further stated that the incident was witnessed by another police officer who was also working the detail, as well as the manager of Honeygrow, Mr. Brian Noparstak (857) 350-3642.

ON 10/21/19 OFFICERS ASSIGNED TO C6 ATTEMPTED TO PLACE JOHN DONOVAN UNDER ARREST FOR WARRANTS. AT 713 EAST BROADWAY. DONOVAN WAS ON THE GROUND AT THE TIME RESISTING ARREST WITH ONE OF HIS HANDS ON HIS HEAD. PO STEELE USED UNAUTHORIZED FORCE. HE USED HIS FOOT AND MADE CONTACT WITH DONOVAN'S HEAD. ¶ About 10:43 am on Monday, 10/21/2019, Officers were dispatched with information over channel 6 from Sergeant Kintigos Z915 of the Boston Housing Police with information that he was driving behind an individual known to him as John Donovan who had an active warrant and a recent BOLO bulletin from the BRIC was released through the department Email. Mr Donovan was operating MA reg/458KF8 a silver Acura 32TL which was also described in the BRIC bulletin. ¶ Sergeant Kintigos advised the officers that he was behind that vehicle at the intersection of Old Colony and Dorchester St and the the suspect was aware of his presence.  Mr Donovan began speeding down Old Colony Ave heading inbound while going through every red light he approached.  Sergeant Hynes and Sergeant Connolly joined in on the pursuit with lights and sirens activated and observed the suspect drive over the sidewalk at D St and Old Colony Ave to avoid being stopped by the police.  The suspect took a right hand turn onto W Seventh St continuing to drive through red lights and stop signs until the officers were advised to discontinue pursuit by Sergeant Hynes for public safety concerns.  During this pursuit the officers observed a dog was in the backseat flailing around the vehicle because of the operators reckless driving. ¶ Minutes later Lieutenant Perkins received a phone call into the base that John Donovan came into Michael Flaherty's election office located on East Broadway threatening his entire staff.  The suspect left the building and headed toward the Stop and Shop parking lot.  Sergeant Hynes observed the suspect walking toward the parking lot and advised the officers nearby to block the suspect in so he could not drive off.  Officers Steele and Goggin in the F602D/F603D units and Officers Hill/Cox in the FG01D unit both parked their department vehicles behind the suspects vehicle so he could not back out.  The suspect put his vehicle in reverse and rammed into the officer's cruisers multiple times.  The officers approached the suspect's vehicle and broke the window in an attempt to stop the operator. The officers opened the door and while attempting to remove the suspect he began using his hands and feet to hit the officers to resist arrest.  The officers were eventually able to remove the suspect and place him in handcuffs on the ground.  The suspect was placed under arrest for two counts of Assault and Battery by means of a Dangerous Weapon, Assault and Battery on a Police Officer, Driving to Endanger, and Animal Cruelty and was then transported to District 4 for booking. ¶ Boston EMS was dispatched to District 4 to clean the suspect's face due to small lacerations suffered from the incident.  Request for immediate threat license Suspension form was completed and faxed to the RMV.  The suspects vehicle MA Reg/458KF8 was towed by Peter's Towing slip#7456.  Numerous Officers were transported to the Hospital for blood exposure.

narrative_x: The following are the details of a complaint made against a police officer by John Garrett(DOB: 11/7/1975, 211 W.56th Street #7C, New York, NY 10019, 310-384-9152). I was notified by the operations division(see P# P210444590) that a person(later identified as Garrett) wanted to file a report about an assault and battery committed by a police officer. The caller was located at the Hyatt Hotel(60 Devonshire St). I responded there and had operations contact Garrett via phone and he met me in the lobby of the hotel. Garrett relayed the following information to me; he stated that he is a tourist visiting from New York and staying at the hotel. Garrett stated that he was out walking looking for a bar that would be open. Garrett stated numerous times that he had a few drinks and was smoking marijuana while walking around. Garrett stated that he saw what appeared to be a film production on Devonshire St a short distance from his hotel and was standing in the general area of the production. Garrett stated that someone he assumed was a member of the film crew told him that he could not stand there and that he did not immediately leave. Garrett stated that he was then approached by an African American male dressed in all black who grabbed him by the throat and he was "pushed half way down the block."    Garrett stated that the man who grabbed him did not say anything to him. Garrett stated that he began to question why the man had touched him and approached a parked Boston Police cruiser that was nearby and the man who had grabbed him told him that it was his. Garrett stated that it was then that he learned the man was a police officer. Garrett stated that the man told him his badge number was 4349. Garrett stated that there was another woman there who he thought was a police officer but did not have on a uniform who witnessed the incident. Garrett described the officer as an black man; approximately the same height as him(5'11"). Garrett stated that this incident happened approximately thirty minutes before he called to report the incident. Garrett stated that he wanted to file a complaint. ¶ I am aware of who the Officer in question is based on the description and the fact that the officer is working at the movie production. I know from earlier in the evening the Police Officer Cornell Patterson of the K-9 unit was working that film production on overtime as he checked in at the station prior to heading to the location.

allegation_x: DV Responsibility of DVU Supervisor | Directives/Orders
narrative_x: Violation of Rule 102 ¶ Section 4 NEGLECT OF DUTY ¶ Section 8 DIRECTIVES AND ORDERS ¶ Failure to adhere to BPD Rules and Procedures, Rule 327A Domestic Violence Situations Involving Department Employees. ¶ Specifically Section 5, Responsibilities of the Domestic Violence Supervisor. ¶ Upon notification from operations of a confirmed incident of domestic violence involving a department employee, the DVU Supervisor shall respond to the scene. ¶ In accordance with MGL c.209A, when a crime involving abuse is committed by a department employee, the DVU Supervisor will take appropriate action including aiding the victim and identifying and arresting the offender. ¶ Failure to obey directives of the Commander of the FJC as transmitted via department email on March 11, 2021 instructing the DVU Supervisors to respond to the scene of all Domestic Incidents which involve a department employee when notified by the Operations Supervisor. narrative_x: I, Lt Gary J Ryan submit the following report. ¶ On November 13th, 2021, Officer Sequan Sparks-Clancy worked a day tour at Area D4. He was assigned as the DD96D (front desk). At approximately 8 am, Officer Sparks-Clancy informed the Duty Supervisor (Sergeant Hogardt) that a woman had come into the station wishing to speak to the supervisor. Sergeant Hogardt spoke with Ms Traganos. Ms Traganos wanted to file a police because she was a victim of a car break. Sergeant Hogardt then directed her to Officer Sparks-Clancy in order for him to complete the report. ¶ Approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes later, Sergeant Hogardt asked Officer Sparks-Clancy if he had completed the report. Officer Sparks-Clancy stated that he hadn't gotten to it yet. At approximately 2 pm (2 hours later), Sergeant Hogardt asked Officer Sparks-Clancy if the report was complete. Officer Sparks-Clancystated that he had not written the report yet, but would finish the report by the end of his tour. Sergeant Hogardt then directed him to do the report. Let it be known, that when Sergeant Hogardt was speaking with Officer Sparks-Clancy, Officer Sparks-Clancy was scrolling through his phone while a movie was playing on the computer. Also, A check of the DD96's unit history for that 8 and a half hour period showed that the report that Sergeant Hogardt was looking for was the only police report generated by Officer Sparks-Clancy that day. ¶ Sergeant Hogardt continued on with his tour of duty and went on to perform a first half at Area D4. A few hours after roll call, Sergent Hogardt was approached by multiple people alerting him of a social media post that was posted by Officer Sparks-Clancy. The caption of the post reads "When your supervisor ask where that report at for the 5th time? Like fool don't you see I'm working". On Thursday, 12/9/21, the complainant, Wesley Ng, reported that he is going through the hiring process for a 911 call taker position in the operations department.  Mr. Ng does not have n department ID, and provided his passport ID upon entry to headquarters at around 11:20 AM for a physical in the 3rd floor.  Mr. Ng stated that he was never issued a badge to proceed to the elevators, activating the alarms, but was directed to proceed to the elevator.  Mr. Ng proceeded to the 3rd.  Mr. Ng stated that he did go downstairs again at one point, to go to the cafeteria, but return to the 3rd floor because he did not have a badge.  After Mr. Ng completed his appointment, he left the building, but later return to get his passport ID.  Officers had switch positions at this point.  Mr. Ng explained to me that a white officer told him that badge cost $35 dollars and would be responsible for the lost.  Mr. Ng stated that for 25 minutes he emptied out his pockets, and empty out his backpack.  At one point nonwhite officer referred to him as "slow, and not all in the head", which sparked Mr. Ng to file a report considering he has dealt with depression and mental health struggles in the past.  Mr. Ng also stated that he did ask the white officer for his name and badge number.  According to Mr. Ng the officer did not provide it because the officer told him that he (Mr. Ng) was in the wrong.  Mr. Ng stated he asked for the badge and number at around 2:12 pm - 2:15 pm.  Mr. Ng describe one officer a white male, 30-40 years old, glasses, bald, no facial hair.  The second officer was non-white, maybe Hispanic, light skin, braids, mustache, glasses.  Mr. Ng also emailed April Davies (Director of HR).  Below is the email that was sent. ¶ Dear April, ¶ Today at 11:20 am, I entered the police department to check-in for my physical. I successfully complied and passed through security check. I walked to the front desk, completed the sign-in form, showed him my passport ID to ask for access to the medical department. The officer, who assisted me, had glasses, a mustache, and braids. He simply directed me to the license desk to get a photocopy of my ID. ¶ After I received my photocopy of my passport ID, I showed it to the officer and he just gave me back the paper back without a badge. He directed me to the third floor and go all the way to the right. I asked for a repeat of instructions because it was hard to hear through the glass and the mask. I went through but the alarm rang. It was probably because I never received a badge so I tried to ask for it and the officer just told me to go through to the elevator. I successfully went to the medical department, met Gina, completed my psych tests at 1:54 pm. ¶ I went downstairs and exited the department but I almost forgot my ID so I went inside. Now the officer, who had assisted me at the front desk, switched places with the officer who was working as security. He told me to go the front desk to get my ID. The white officer at the front desk told me that I cannot get my ID unless I have the badge to the medical department. However I was never given a badge. I did not even know what color the badge looked like because I was never given one. The officer then stated that I was lying and accused me of going to the second floor by accident. I never did that. ¶ The officer, with braids and glasses, told his fellow officer that I did receive a badge and that I was not all there in the head. That offended me greatly because I struggled with mental health problems in the past and I felt like he was belittling me as someone who had a mental deficit. The officer then walked away. ¶ It was now 2:05 pm and the officers refused to give me my ID. The white officer stated that the badge costs $35 and I could be responsible for this charge. The white officer then told me to take everything out of my bag, my jacket, jean, and shirt pockets. I did so because they were the police. I had no other choice. After 2:20 pm, the white officer told me that I could leave. I wanted to get their names and badge ID but they did not show these items to me. ¶ I finally left the department and I was crying on my way home because of what had happened. I would like to know where I could file this report because this was just not okay. ¶ I apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for taking the time to read this email. ¶ Sincerely, ¶ Wesley Ng

narrative_x: On Wednesday, January 5, 2022, Denise Merlino assigned to the Paid Details Payment Unit informed me that an email was received from Timothy Halikias, Finance Coordinator, of Accutemp Engineering Inc stating the following: ¶ “Good Morning, ¶ I hope you are doing well. ¶ I am emailing you regarding invoice #BPD0098037. We originally requested two officers at 7am for this paid detail, but only one officer arrived at 9:30am and only one slip was signed according to the job foreman on site. We paid for the officer that arrived under invoice #BPD0097413, but now we are being billed for the 2nd officer that never arrived. ¶ Can you please help us with this?” ¶ I directed Ms. Merlino to forward the email to me, and I would contact Mr. Halikias to discuss his concern.  Prior to contacting Mr. Halikias, I found that the details in question were assigned tracking numbers 2467807 and 2467808.  The details were assigned to Officers Eliana Builes and Kato Francis respectively, and the scheduled start time for each was 08:00 hours, and the scheduled end time was 14:00 hours. The details were to be conducted at 88 Kingston Street on District A-1 on October 26, 2021. ¶ Both details were assigned the day of the detail. Officer Builes was assigned the detail at 08:47 hours and Officer Francis was assigned the detail at 09:19 hours. ¶ Upon review of the details, I found discrepancies with the submitted detail cards. ¶ 1.	The detail card submitted by Officer Builes has a start time of 09:00 hours, and an end time of 9:45 hours for a total of 45 minutes worked and the detail card is checked “No Show.” The ¶ detail card was signed with a signature of “Jenkins.” ¶ 2.	The detail card submitted by Officer Francis has a start time of 09:30 hours, and an end time of 14:00 hours for a total of 4 ½ hours worked. The detail card was signed with a signature of ¶ “Dante Defuria.” ¶ 3.	Officer Builes’ end time of 09:45 hours is after the start time indicated on Officer Francis’ detail card of 09:30 hours (15 minutes after). ¶ Note: ¶ 1.	Officer Builes’ detail card was verified on December 8, 2021, 43 days after the detail was performed. ¶ 2.	Officer Francis’ detail card was verified on October 28, 2021, 2 days after the detail was performed. ¶ After review of the detail cards, I contacted Mr. Halikias.  Per our conversation, he stated the Accutemp Engineering does not have an employee by the name of “Jenkins” and Accutemp Engineering only had one detail officer work on October 26, 2021. Mr. Halikias also stated that Officer Francis who performed the detail was released shortly after he arrived due to the crane work being completed and there was no longer a need for a detail, but Mr. Defuria, construction supervisor, signed Officer Francis out for the scheduled end time of 2:00 PM.  Mr. Halikias stated he would get the approximate time Officer Francis was released. ¶ I requested that Mr. Halikias document our conversation and submit it to me in an email. Mr. Halikias stated he would after he spoke with Mr. Defuria about Officer Francis’ end time and we concluded our conversation. ¶ On January 6, 2021, I received an email from Mr. Halikias that stated the following: ¶ “Good Morning Marcus, ¶ It was a pleasure speaking with you yesterday. ¶ I spoke with our Construction Supervisor, Dante Defuria Jr, who was on site on Oct 26 and signed the detail authorization record for Officer Francis. He provided me with the following information: ¶ •	We requested two police officers for the detail ¶ •	Officer Francis arrived at 9:30am and was on site for approx. 1.5-2 hours. He mentioned to Dante that he was late because he was out of district ¶ •	Officer Builes never arrived as far as we know and we do not have an employee with the first or last name Jenkins. We’re not sure why it was marked as a no show since we had workers ¶ on site starting at 6am until 2pm ¶ If you need any additional information, please don’t hesitate to contact me directly.” ¶ After reviewing the email, I again contacted Mr. Halikias with regard to Officer Francis being released early.  Mr. Halikias stated that he would address the end time specified on the detail card and the actual time Officer Francis was released.  I later received an email that stated the following: ¶ “Good Morning Marcus, ¶ It was a pleasure speaking with you yesterday. ¶ I spoke with our Construction Supervisor, Dante Defuria Jr, who was on site on Oct 26 and signed the detail authorization record for Officer Francis. He provided me with the following information: ¶ •	We requested two police officers for the detail ¶ •	Officer Francis arrived at 9:30am. He was on site until approx. 11-11:30am, but the detail authorization record shows an end time of 2pm. We were under the impression that we would be ¶ invoiced for 4 hours, but we were invoiced for 8 hours total ¶ •	Officer Builes never arrived as far as we know and we do not have an employee with the first or last name Jenkins. We’re not sure why it was marked as a no show since we had workers ¶ on site from 6am until 2pm” ¶ After reviewing the details in question and after corresponding with Mr. Halikias, Officer Eliana Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467807 and checked “No Show” on the card and did not submit it to the appropriate detail clerk in a timely fashion (96 hours) as required under Special Order 15-014 and Special Order 18-031.  The detail card was received 43 days after the scheduled date of the detail for compensation. ¶ The vendor Accutemp Engineering has no record of Officer Builes performing the detail and the construction supervisor stated that he only signed the detail card for the officer that was present. If Officer Builes arrived at the assigned detail at 09:00 hours and signed out of the assigned detail at 09:45 hours, she would have been at the assigned location when Officer Francis arrived at 09:30 hours. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Builes was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 09:00 and an actual end time of 09:45 hours as true and accurate.  Officer Builes was also Untruthful by marking the detail card that Accutemp Engineering was a "No Show." ¶ •	Officer Builes’ submitted detail card is in direct conflict with the detail card submitted by Officer Kato Francis and is supported by Mr. Timothy Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stating only ¶ one officer performed the detail at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Builes’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467807 with a start time of 09:00 hours and an end time of 09:45 hours. Accutemp Engineering knowing only one ¶ officer performed the detail coupled with the fact the construction crew was on-site from 06:00 hours to 14:00 hours, caused Accutemp Engineering to question the invoice.  Officer Builes’ ¶ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by contractor and the general public.  It gives the false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect ¶ compensation for a detail that was not worked. ¶ Officer Builes violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card for verification until 43 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Builes was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days). ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467807 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  Accutemp Engineering does not have any record of Officer ¶ Builes working the assigned detail at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Builes submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467807 for indication that she had performed the detail, but not having performed the assigned detail at 88 Kingston ¶ Street on October 26, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ As a result of reviewing the invoice in question with regard to Officer Builes’ detail card submission, it was discovered that Officer Kato Francis submitted a detail card that was not reflective of the hours worked. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Francis was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 09:30 and an actual end time of 14:00 hours as true and accurate. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ submitted detail card is in direct conflict with the statement by Mr. Timothy Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stating that Officer Francis was released between 11:00-11:30 hours. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards) ¶ •	Officer Francis knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467808 with an ending time that was not reflective of the actual time he was released and submitted a detail card ¶ with an 09:30 hours start and an 14:00 hours finish time. Mr. Halikias stated that Officer Francis was released at approximately 11:00-11:30 hours. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ detail card should have reflected working a maximum of 2 hours worked for a minimum of 4 hours paid.  By allowing his card to reflect 4 ½ hours worked, he was paid for 8 ¶ hours worked. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467808 for indication that he had performed the detail until 14:00 hours, but having been released between 11:00-11:30 ¶ hours at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Francis did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467808 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  Mr. Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stated Officer Francis ¶ was released prior to 14:00 hours. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Francis’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Francis knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467808 with a start time of 09:30 hours and an end time of 14:00 hours. Dante Defuria, construction supervisor, ¶ released Officer Francis between 11:00-11:30 hours but signed Officer Francis’ detail card for a 14:00 hour end time.  Officer Francis’ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by ¶ contractor and the general public.  It gives the false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect compensation for hours not actual hours worked.

narrative_x: As a result of a preliminary detail investigation that was conducted on Wednesday, January 5, 2022, into a questioned invoice by Accutemp Engineering with regard to Officer Eliana Builes, I performed another preliminary investigation with regard to an assigned detail for RJV Construction Corporation performed on August 23, 2021 at 4 Falcon Street on District A-7. ¶ A request for two officers was made by Mr. Victor Pacella, Project Manager, for RJV Construction.  The detail was assigned to Officers Eliana Builes and John Pels on the day of the detail, August 23, 2021.  The details were assigned at 08:25 hours and 09:45 hours respectively. ¶ Officer Builes submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441604, with a start time of 08:30 hours and an end time of 09:00 hours and marked the detail card “No Show” for a total of 30 minutes worked. ¶ Officer Pels submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441605, with a start time of 10:15 hours and an end time of 15:00 hours for a total of 4 hours and 45 minutes worked. ¶ Note: ¶ 1.	Officer Builes’ detail card was verified on October 6, 2021, 44 days after the detail was performed. ¶ 2.	Officer Pels’ detail card was verified on September 2, 2021, 10 days after the detail was performed. ¶ After reviewing the detail card submissions, I contacted Mr. Victor Pacella at RJV Construction about the assigned details.  Mr. Pacella stated that their records indicate that only one officer worked the assigned detail at 4 Falcon Street on August 23, 2021.  Mr. Pacella also stated the construction crew worked the entire day from 07:30 hours to 15:00 hours. ¶ Based on our conversation, I requested that Mr. Pacella document our conversation in writing on a department letter head, scan, and email to me.  Mr. Pacella was concerned about the response the RJV Construction would receive from police officers if he documented the reported issue.  I informed Mr. Pacella that the Boston Police Department would investigate any reported misconduct.  Mr. Pacella stated he would provide the requested letter with supporting documents. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Builes was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 08:30 and an actual end time of 09:00 hours as true and accurate. Officer Builes was also untruthful by marking “No Show” on the detail card. ¶ •	Officer Builes’ detail card submission is in direct conflict to the hours worked by RJV Construction.  RJV started work at 07:30 hours and worked until 15:00 hours. Coupled with the fact ¶ that Officer John Pels did work the assigned detail. Officer Builes’ submission of a “No Show” detail card reflecting she performed the detail from 08:30-09:00 hours cannot be accurate ¶ giving RJV was on-site at 07:30 hours and Officer Pels arrived at 10:15 hours. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). narrative_x: I came home around 3am on 3/19/22 to find a Ford Edge SUV, MA plate number 223 D70, parked in my driveway halfway on my lawn. I called two tow truck companies and was told they couldn't tow a trespass unless it was ok'd by BPD. I called the non emergency number and they told me they would send an officer out to my address. After waiting half an hour I called again. An officer showed up around 4:10. At that time I called the tow truck company, the officer made sure that I was willing to pay for the vehicle to be towed and I put the tow company on speaker so the officer could approve the tow. On Thursday April 7, 2022 I was in attendance of the Compstat Meeting on the first floor of Boston Police Headquarters in the Media Room.  Upon conclusion of the regular Compstat Meeting there was a meeting directly following.  The second meeting was held to review the Boston Police Departments Operations Plan for the 2022 Boston Marathon to be held on Monday April 18, 2022. BFS Deputy Superintendent James Tarantino was conducting the meeting.  Those in attendance were the members of the Boston Police Command Staff  including Superintendents, Deputy Superintendents, District Captains and Lieutenants.  There were four monitors that were being used to display the Operations Plan to all in attendance.  Deputy Tarantino proceeded to give instructions and address the Commanders of each Zone directly. I was the assigned as the Zone 4 Commander. Other commanders on the plan being displayed for Zone 4 were Captain Detective Terry Thomas who had been assigned to MIS for some time and would not be on active duty.  Deputy C. Walsh was also assigned to Zone 4 however, he was not in attendance of this meeting. My name was on the monitor underneath Captain Detective Thomas and Deputy C. Walsh.  Deputy Tarantino started to speak of the assignments concerning Zone 4 and addressed D-14 Captain Mark Harrington directly disregarding the plan and me.  Captain Harrington corrected Deputy Tarantino and advised him that he was not assigned to Zone 4.  The four monitors again were on display in plain sight for all in attendance to view. Deputy Tarantino continued to disrespect me by not acknowledging my presence even after I announced to him "Deputy I am right here" for all in the room to hear I was not recognized by him.  He proceeded to review the plan directly addressing all the Zone Commanders in attendance by name. For the record I had spent many years of my career assigned to BFS Area D-4 and had been a supervisor with experience having been assigned to many past Boston Marathons throughout.  I was also well aware of the high priority of ensuring public safety for Zone 4 considering the 2013 Terrorist Bombing Event which had taken place in Zone 4.  I also had knowledge of the Zone 4 area being the highest area of spectators attending the event. ¶ The public display of disrespect and hostility towards me by Deputy Tarantino was humiliating.  As the meeting progressed Deputy Tarantino went on to speak about sworn members of the Boston Police Department who would not be working because they submitted personal leave days.  He loudly exclaimed in a strong vile derogatory tone that those individuals were ¶ "PUSSY'S" !   Upon him saying  "PUSSY'S" most of the room which consisted of an all male command staff (other than one female) proceeded to laugh.  At this point I was in emotional shock at what had just taken place.  It was surreal as I felt confused, humiliated, offended, angry and ridiculed all at the same time and not only from the word "PUSSY'S"  but from the laughing response of most all of the male command staff in the room.  I witnessed them laugh at such a vile vulgarity,  a derogatory and demeaning  slang word describing female anatomy.  I could not speak as I had no words at the time.  Not one individual in the meeting had the decorum to corrected Deputy Tarantino, they all allowed this unprofessional behavior.  As I had made my presence known earlier in this meeting I am certain the Deputy was well aware a female was present.  When the meeting concluded shortly after I left the room visibly upset. I do believe some of the Command Staff at that point took notice.  I noticed that Deputy Tarantino had called my department cell phone later that day and left me a voice message admitting he used colorful language and went on to say he had meant to say "SISSY'S" which I found equally offensive.  I have taken a long time to reflect on this incident.  However, as the highest ranking civil service female sworn member, I have concluded that it is incumbent upon me as a leader to document this incident not only for me but for all females who serve or will serve on the Boston Police Department. With the hopes that no one will be discriminated against due to their gender.  I have worked to serve the Boston Police Department throughout my long dedicated career in the most professional and respectful manner and I would expect the same from those who serve alongside me.  I was promoted to the rank of Captain in 2018 and at this time as well as in 2018,  I am still the only female at this level of command.  Prior to 2018 the last female to be promoted to Captain was in 2005.  I have served our department well and worked my way through the ranks serving in the most busy district stations( D-4, D-14, B-2, A-1, E-13, E-18, E-5).  Much of my time was spent on various shifts.  I am now assigned to the Boston Police Family Justice Center in the role as a Captain Detective.  The units which I command at the FJC investigate crimes primarily against woman and it is especially rewarding to be able to serve these victims.  I am proud of my accomplishments as a Female member of the Boston Police Department.  I recently attended POST Training which was required.  During the training there was a course called "Bystander Training" and promoted intervention for workplace Sexual Harassment. That training has afforded me the strength and courage  to report this incident in which I experienced so much disrespect that I have questioned my effectiveness in my role on this department. I would like to ensure that future female leaders on the Boston Police Department do not endure a Hostile Work Environment, Discrimination or Sexual Harassment. ¶ I therefore ask that an investigation be conducted and charge a rule violation did occur specifically: ¶ Rule 114. Sexual Harassment, Discrimination, Harassment, and Retaliation Policy and Complaint Procedure ¶ Section 3 B Harassment (Hostile Work Environment) - Harassment is a form of discrimination. Harassing conduct of any type (oral, written, graphic or physical) directed against a person because of his or her race, color, gender, national origin/ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, parental status, disability or gender identity and expression, and which unreasonably interferes with the person’s work or creates a work environment that a reasonable person would find hostile, offensive, humiliating or intimidating.

I answered some, then stopped when they became inappropriate. Mind you, I was totally caught off guard by the fact this this police officer was now interacting with me 20min later in a completely different location and am shocked by the fact that he found me. He asked "Are you always in this much of a rush?" "What do you do for work?", "How old are you?", "Are you single?, "Are you dating someone?", "Do you ever have time to date?". I responded that I was not interested in dating and felt very uncomfortable having a uniformed police officer asking me these questions. He asked if we could grab "coffee" sometime and I said no. I then ask him why he was following me, if this was his territory and what his name was. He said that "it didn't matter". I told him that I needed to go and proceeded to walk away in the opposite direction, but it did not end there…I turn a corner and hide behind a parked car because I am worried he will see me again.
