On Sunday, August 7, 2022 Sgt. Best entered an ACISS log note (22-13821) which indicated "EBH ¶ Investigations advises GEU of a cash theft that occurred at 0300 hours. Suspect picked up victim's ¶ wallet, removed $200 from it, then gave wallet to hotel registration and departed property. Investigations ¶ will attempt to contact suspect and contact GEU if additional assistance is needed." ¶ 2. On Monday, August 8, 2022, EBH Investigators contacted me after business hours regarding this ¶ same larceny. This larceny appeared to be handled in the normal course of manner by EBH ¶ Investigations with no GEU involvement besides GEU being notified. At this time, An EBH Investigator ¶ informed me that a member of the EBH Surveillance Team notified the Security Investigations Team ¶ that the larceny suspect was possibly a Boston Police Officer. This suspect had been previously ¶ identified by EBH Investigators as Rebecca Julia Leo 5/20/90. I advised the Investigator that I currently ¶ did not have access to review the video and I would review it on Tuesday, August 9 th . ¶ 3. The following day I located and viewed a video clip stored in the Surveillance Locker with a Clip ¶ Number of 34136 titled "Wallet Theft 31BZ07" and Incident ID of IN20220021105. The following is a ¶ summary of events I observed while watching video clips: ¶ · Camera 3198 @ 02:31:40 hrs. the victim's wallet falls from his left pocket. The victim is wearing a blue ¶ shirt and is wearing a baseball hat backwards. ¶ · Camera 3198 @ 02:46:48 hrs. Leo appears to see the wallet on the floor and picks it up. allegation_x: Training and Qualifications | Reporting firearm Discharges
narrative_x: On 8/19/2022, it was reported to Scituate PD that there had an accidental discharge in Detective Rodney Best's home located at 14 Utility Road in Scituate. Scituate PD was not notified nor was Boston PD notified in a timely manner in violation of  Rule 303, Section 11 which states: ¶ Sec. 10 Reporting Firearms Discharges: All firearm discharges, except discharges which occur during Department authorized or approved firearms training, while lawfully engaged in target practice or while hunting (unless a discharge occurring during one of these three exceptions results in death, personal injury or property damage), require the submission of an incident report (1.1) which includes information relative to injuries and damage to property. ¶ An officer who discharges his firearm during the course of his duties shall immediately notify the Operations Division that they have been involved in a “Code 303” and request that a Patrol Supervisor respond to the scene. The officer shall make a verbal report of ¶ the discharge to the responding Patrol Supervisor. In the event that someone has been injured, officers will request medical assistance. The supervisor shall request that Operations make all appropriate notifications including the Firearm Discharge Investigation Team. ¶ An off-duty officer discharging a firearm in the City of Boston shall immediately notify an Operations Division Supervisor. The Operations Division shall notify the Officer in Charge of the District in which the discharge took place and the Firearm Discharge Investigation ¶ The officer involved in the firearm discharge shall submit the necessary reports without delay to a Superior Officer assigned to the Firearm Discharge Investigation Team. ¶ An officer who discharges a weapon outside of the City of Boston shall immediately notify and make a report of the discharge to the Police Department which has jurisdiction where the discharge occurred, identify themself as being a Boston police officer and notify an Operations Division Supervisor as soon as possible. The Operations Division shall immediately notify the officer’s Commanding Officer and the Firearm Discharge Investigation Team. ¶ Officers who have discharged a firearm shall complete a BPD Form 2415 (Firearms Discharge Report) in its entirety. ¶ On 8/19/2022, it was reported to Scituate PD that there had an accidental discharge in Detective Rodney Best's home located at 14 Utility Road in Scituate. Mr. William Hofmockel call IAD and spoke with S/D Hanson. During the conversation, Mr. Hofmockel stated on August 17th, 2022, at 4:30 p.m., he was walking in the parking lot of Stop & Shop, at 545 Freeport Ave. when a motorist almost hit him. Mr. Hofmockel articulated that as the vehicle came close to him he slapped the driver's window. He conveyed that he believed the vehicle was speeding through the parking lot and was traveling in excess of 20 m.p.h. when it almost hit him.  The vehicle stopped. Mr. Hofmockel identified the license plate of the vehicle as MA Registration 2LHG59. He also provided his license plate as MA Registration 1EWY17.  When the driver rolled the window down they exchange words. Mr. Hofmockel disclosed he cursed and called the driver names.  Mr. Hofmockel revealed that the vehicle was operated by a female.  Mr. Hofmockel said he then walked away and entered the store and began to shop.  While inside Stop & Shop he was approached by a female Boston Police Officer (see P#220374727).  Officer Lopes (ID#148288) helped mediated the situation.  Mr. Hofmockel stated apologies were exchanged and all parties then left the area.  Mr. Hofmockel stated he thought the incident was behind him.  Then on September 14, 2022, Mr. Hofmockel's employer received a telephone call from a person who identified himself as Retired Boston Police Detective Bobby Roger.  Det. Roger told his employer (Old Town Realty) that he was well connected and could get things done. Det. Rogers revealed he is a former S.W.A.T. team member.  He ended their conversation by saying nobody is going to treat his daughter like that.  Mr. Hofmockel stated he was concerned for his safety and questioned how Det. Roger was able to learn his identity and his place of employment.  A CJIS check of Mr. Hofmockel's vehicle was conducted which revealed that his vehicle was queried on August 17th, 2022, by Detective William Parlon.

(see I#222079943). ¶ The caller/ victim, Jaquelyn Giblin, informed the 911 call taker that her husband Gerard Giblin was being aggressive and was throwing items in the house. She also advised the call taker he had left home. ¶ On arrival, Mrs. Giblin was outside the residence and met the Officers in the driveway as Officers attempted to ascertain information about what had occurred. Mrs. Giblin immediately requested that she not be recorded (referencing the Officer's Body Worn Cameras). Mrs. Giblin stated, "I want to cancel any audio or video recording, please." At this point, the Officer informed BPD Operations that they would be Code 29. Mrs. Giblin reported to the Officers that her husband had left in his truck, but she wasn't sure of the registration plate information. The Officers obtained the registration information from a registry check through CJIS via the MDT in the cruiser. ¶ Mrs. Gibllin stated that he started throwing things about the house, broke a door, punched a picture causing the glass to break, and knocked over a heater on the back deck. Upon entering the residence, the Officers observed that the house was in complete disarray. The Officers observed clothes, food items, broken glass, knocked-over furniture, and a towel with what appeared to be blood in the kitchen, living room, and hallway areas. Mrs. Giblin informed the Officers that her husband had injured his hand during his outburst. Mrs. Giblin informed the Officers that their children, a six-year-old son, a three-year-old daughter, and an eight-month daughter, were present when he had his outburst, but she was not sure exactly where they were or what they saw during the incident. narrative_x: I respectfully report that Officer Bryan Augustine, I.D.# 148242, violated Boston Police Department Rules and Procedures, Rule 102, Section 10, Eight Counts. ¶ Officer Augustine called in sick on July 9, 15, and August 6, 2022.  He exhausted all of his sick time and vacation before July 9.  As a result, Officer Augustine was carried as AWOL for the above dates. ¶ On August 6, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick at 11:37 PM, failing to provide sufficient time before the beginning of his shift. ¶ On August 14, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report for duty on time and had to be woken up by a supervisor. ¶ On October 16, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for his regularly scheduled tour of duty and failed to notify a supervisor. ¶ On October 19, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick after the start of his regularly scheduled tour of duty and was carried as AWOL. ¶ Counts 1, 2, and 3 - Officer Augustine violated Boston Police Rule 102, Section 10 - Unauthorized Absence from Duty, by calling in sick when he had exhausted his sick time and vacation time; attachment # 1 is (an email from John Brennan verifying the dates).  Officer Augustine had four personal days at the time of the absences but chose to call in sick. As a result, he carried AWOL for those dates.  He also violated Boston Police Department Rule 102, Section 10, Counts 4, 5, 6, and 7 by failing to report for duty on time. ¶ Count 4 - On August 6, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick seven minutes prior to the beginning of his shift, not allowing reasonable and timely notice, attachment #2 (Sergeant DeFeo’s report). ¶ Count 5 - On August 14, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report for duty at the start of his shift, 2345 hours, and had to be woken up by a supervisor, attachment #3 and #4 (Sergeant Swan and Sergeant Minichello reports). ¶ Count 6 - On October 16, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for duty again and did not notify a supervisor prior to being late, attachment #5 and #6 (Sergeant Swan and Officer Sosa’s reports). ¶ Officer Augustine filed a Form 26 concerning the August 14 and October 16 incidents.  He reported that he was late but did not provide a reasonable explanation as to why nor why he did not notify a supervisor, attachments #7 and #8 (Officer Augustine’s reports). ¶ Count 7 - On October 18, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for his scheduled tour of duty.  He called in sick at 2350 hours when his scheduled tour began at 23:45; attachments #9 and #10 (Audio recording and Sergeant Minichello’s report). ¶ Count 8 - Officer Augustine called in sick on October 18, 2022, without having any sick time available.  He was AWOL for the tour, attachment #11 (Absence Report) ¶ Officer Augustine received a notice of excessive sick time abuse by Captain John Greland while assigned to District 13 on February 27, 2020, warning him that continuation of sick time abuse may result in a suspension without pay, attachment #12 (Excessive Sick Leave Report). Officer Augustine has continually demonstrated a lack of attentiveness toward his time and attendance as a Boston Police Officer.  His current pattern is evidence of complete unawareness or total disregard for his actions, placing his fellow officers and the unit at risk. Therefore, in keeping with the concept of progressive discipline, I issued Officer Augustine a 1-day suspension. ¶ I presented Officer Augustine with the Notice of Suspension, BPD Form 0016-BFS-1005, on Thursday, October 20, 2022, in a meeting with Sergeant McGillicuddy and BPPA Union Representative Officer Conway.  He was also given a copy of M.G.L Chapter 31, Section 41, along with a copy of Boston Police Department Rule 102.  Officer Augustine waved his rights to request a hearing and signed the waiver.  His suspension will commence on October 22, 2022.

narrative_x: On October 10, 2020, ACD received an email alleging that there is often a marked Boston Police cruiser parked at 259 Bennington St. near the rear door of La Chiva Restaurant after closing time (3:00 am).  The complainant would usually see the unoccupied cruiser between 4:30 and 6:30 am.  La Chiva had recently hired C.I. Security for the late-night crowds.  C.I. Security was the subject of an unrelated ACD investigation. ¶ ACD initiated an investigation to determine the officer's whereabouts and if the officer had any involvement with C.I. Security.  ACD investigators conducted surveillance from October 13 until November 22, 2022, and received additional emails from the complainant on October 16 and November 14 with photos of a cruiser parked near La Chiva’s back door.  Investigators identified Officer Michael Forde, ID# 8847.  Forde is assigned to District A-1 and frequently works morning watch overtime in District A-7.  The investigation revealed that although Forde parked near La Chiva, he did not enter the restaurant.  However, investigators discovered that Forde was going into a residence located at 237 Bennington St., likely on the second floor, and taking his calls from there.  Sometimes, Forde would hold onto Code 19s in other locations while inside the dwelling.  The mailbox indicates the second-floor tenants are Karolina Posada and Brayan Ventura Posada. ¶ The investigation revealed no evidence of criminal activity on the part of Officer Forde.  However, it exposed the following potential administrative violations: ¶ On November 4, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G416A on overtime.  Forde was inside 237 Bennington St. at 1:00 am on November 5 when he was dispatched to 53 Putnam St. for a fight (P220512063).  Investigators observed Forde walk to and enter his cruiser which was parked at 257 Bennington St. at the bus stop and drive toward Day Square.  At 3:10 am, Forde was dispatched to 336 Saratoga St. for a DVIP (P220512202).  A query of evidence.com revealed that Forde did not activate his body-worn camera at either call. ¶ On November 17, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G201A on overtime with Officer Paula Pearson.  At 1:52 am on November 18, Forde and Pearson were dispatched to 142 Marginal St. for a BEIP.  During this call, neither Forde nor Pearson activated their body-worn cameras. ¶ On November 21, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G425A on overtime.  At 12:43 am on November 22, Forde self-initiated a Code 19 over the air at Sumner St. and Liverpool St. (P220540855). At 01:21, investigators observed a marked cruiser pull up and park in front of 249 Bennington St.  Forde exited the cruiser wearing a black civilian jacket and black knit hat and walked toward 237 Bennington St.  Although he was inside this apartment, Forde held onto the Code 19 and was eventually cleared by the dispatcher at 3:06 am.  At 3:22 am, Forde was dispatched to 810 Border St. for a BEIP (P220540945).  At about 3:23 am, the interior lights turned on from the second floor of 237 Bennington St.  At 3:26 am, Forde exited the front door of 237, walked to his cruiser, and responded to the call with blue lights activated. On Sunday, December 11, 2022, there was an incident involving Sergeant DeFeo, I.D. # 11598, and Officer Augustine.  Officer Augustine was scheduled to work his regular Day Tour on December 11, 2022.  At 7:45 AM, Sergeant DeFeo called the Front Desk and spoke to Officer Murphy, I.D. # 131263, and inquired if Officer Augustine had arrived to work.  Officer Augustine had not.  He arrived around 8:20 AM, according to Sergeant DeFeo’s report. ¶ Sergeant DeFeo proceeded to the Front Desk to challenge Officer Augustine and have him file a report concerning his tardiness when he noticed Officer Augustine's motor vehicle.  Sergeant DeFeo stated in his report that he had addressed Officer Augustine about the tint on the front windshield two previous times, and Officer Augustine failed to correct the issue.  Sergeant DeFeo proceeded to issue Officer Augustine a motor vehicle citation.  During that exchange, Sergeant DeFeo requested a B-2 officer to report to headquarters in order to assist with recording Officer Augustine’s motor vehicle with a Body Worn Camera.  Officer Kerrigan, I.D # 148281, responded.  Sergeant DeFeo issued a motor vehicle violation to Officer Augustine and filed a report concerning the incident. ¶ Officer Augustine met with Lieutenant DiGirolamo and Sergeant McGillicuddy on Monday, December 12, 2022.  According to Lieutenant DiGirolamo and Sergeant McGilliuddy's reports, Officer Augustine expressed concerns over being targeted by Sergeant DeFeo.  He argued that other police officers are late for work and have tinted windows on their personal vehicles, yet they are not addressed by Sergeant DeFeo.  Officer Augustine had photographs to prove his point.  Officer Augustine also alleged that Sergeant DeFeo used profanity while addressing him, and the situation made him feel uncomfortable coming to work.  Lieutenant DiGirolamo did provide Officer Augustine with a copy of Rule 114 and explained the complaint process. narrative_x: On Sunday, March 06, 2022, at approximately 1:40 am, Sgt. Det. Brian Leahy contacted Sgt. Det. Lucas Taxter and informed him that he had just observed Police Officer Matthew Morrissey in front of his home on Chickatawbut St. in Dorchester.  At the time, Officer Morrissey was under investigation by members of the Anti-Corruption Division (ACD), had been interviewed at ACD twice, and had just been placed on administrative leave hours earlier on the morning of March 5 by Sgt. Det. Leahy, Sgt. Det. Taxter, and Lt. Det. Sean Martin. ¶ Sgt. Det. Leahy stated that he observed blue lights coming through his windows approximately ten minutes earlier.  At approximately 1:34 am, Leahy looked out of his front door to see what had happened and observed a black pickup truck stopped in the middle of the street near the end of his driveway.  The vehicle then traveled backward toward Leahy’s front door, and Leahy immediately recognized the registration plate, Mass. Reg. 5BB135, and the vehicle to be the 2019 Chevy Silverado owned by Officer Morrissey.  From within the house, Leahy observed the operator roll down his window, and at that time, he could see that it was Morrissey behind the wheel.  Morrissey had parked the truck on the sidewalk directly in front of Leahy’s front door, facing on-coming traffic and in a no parking zone.  Morrissey’s vehicle was parked approximately ten feet from the front door of Leahy’s house, close enough to block the egress of anyone entering or exiting the home.  From this proximity, Morrissey remained and stared at Leahy, standing in his house behind a glass storm door for approximately one and one-half (1.5) minutes, and then drove away.  Morrissey did not say anything or exit his vehicle.  As Morrissey drove away, Leahy photographed the truck and registration plate with his cellphone.  Sgt. Det. Leahy did not confront Officer Morrissey during this incident. ¶ This was the third in a series of confrontations instigated by Officer Morrissey while he was being investigated for violating the City’s residency ordinance.  On October 26, 2021, Sgt. Det. Leahy was in his assigned department vehicle conducting surveillance of Morrissey from the nearly-empty parking lot of Venezia Restaurant at 20 Ericsson Street, Dorchester.  At approximately 9:05 am, Leahy observed Morrissey’s black Silverado drive toward him and stop about twenty feet away, facing him.  The Silverado then slowly drove past Leahy, turned, and parked perpendicular to him, where it remained for about two minutes.  Because of heavy rain and the Silverado’s tinted windows, Leahy could not see who was operating.  However, a subsequent investigation revealed that Morrissey queried Leahy’s registration plate at 9:08 am on CJIS using his cellphone.  It is believed that this was a counter-surveillance technique used by Morrissey to help determine the extent of the ACD investigation.  Investigators discovered that Morrissey inappropriately queried vehicles registered to him, his family members, and ACD approximately fifty-five times as a counter-surveillance technique. ¶ On November 5, 2021, Sgt. Det. Leahy was again conducting surveillance from 20 Ericsson Street.  As Leahy entered the parking lot at 7:13 pm, he observed Morrissey’s Silverado parked on Ericsson Street facing Walnut Street and the entrance of the lot.  Leahy parked his department vehicle in a parking spot and immediately watched the Silverado enter the parking lot and very slowly encircle his vehicle at least twice from the adjacent travel lanes.  The Silverado did not travel anywhere else in the lot and exited.  Again, due to the window tint, Morrissey wasn’t visible to Leahy.  However, this is the only vehicle ACD investigators have seen Morrissey operate. ¶ The incidents mentioned above have caused great concern for Sgt. Det. Leahy and his family.  While knowingly being investigated by superior officers assigned to the Anti-Corruption Division, Officer Matthew Morrissey deliberately attempted to harass, intimidate, and cause emotional injury to Sgt. Det. Brian Leahy, his family, and to some extent, other members of ACD.  Moreover, Officer Morrissey’s intentional actions on March 6, 2022, while in front of Sgt. Det. Leahy’s home was retaliatory and directly related to being placed on administrative leave approximately fifteen hours earlier. ¶ As a result, on Sunday, March 6, 2022, at about 8:00 pm, Sgt.  Dets. Taxter and Leahy met Milton police officers at 449 Pleasant St, Milton, and placed Morrissey under arrest.  Morrissey was transported to District C-11, booked, and charged with intimidation of a witness/police officer, c268 s13B. Edward McCarthy of Boston EMS/Health and Hospitals (785 Albany Street tel 617-343-1144) came to E-18 at about 1830 hours to file a complaint against Officer Dwayne Jackson (ID #011526). Lt McCarthy reported two of the EMT's he supervises, Robert Donovan and Casey Knowles stated to him Officer Jackson refused to ride in the back of the ambulance during transport of a female EDP who was under the influence of crack cocaine. The EMT's both told Lt McCarthy the female EDP (Ms. Kenyatta Starkes DOB 2-14-1984) was acting in a hostile/combative manner at the scene of the sick assist call at 50 Roanoke Road in Hyde Park. They stated they were both concerned for their safety and asked Officer Jackson to ride in back. They stated Officer Jackson refused to do so and said he would follow behind and assist them if needed. Lt. McCarthy stated they then attempted to transport the female to The Faulkner Hospital. They reported at some point during the transport the female became assaultive and struck EMT Robert Donovan in the forehead with a backhand strike. The strike caused a small cut/laceration to the middle of Mr. Donovan's forehead. EMTs reported they pulled the ambulance over and with the assistance of Officer Jackson they were able to get the female under control. They reported they again asked Officer Jackson to ride in the back of the ambulance for safety reasons. They stated he refused saying ' we are nearly there'. ¶ Lt McCarthy reports both EMTs said shortly before they were pulling into the wagon bay the female bit EMT Robert Donovan on his forearm. Lt McCarthy showed Lt Walsh photos he had taken of both the injuries to Mr. Donovan with his department phone. I advised him to save the photos. The injuries were clearly visible in the photos and the forearm injury was consistent with a human bite with teeth marks clearly visible. Lt McCarthy informed Lt Walsh he would be completing an injured on duty report for EMT Robert Donovan. The EMTs said when they prepared to transport the female form the ambulance into the emergency room they requested Officer Jackson handcuff her. Lt McCarthy states he told them he would seek flexy cuffs from Faulkner Hospital Security Officer. They reported the security guard (David Westin tel 617-983-7677) did not have any flexy cuffs. Lt McCarthy reports the EMTS with assistance from EMTS Kevin Pywell and John Markoast were able to secure the female into a room in the emergency area. Lt McCarthy stated EMT Donovan request Officer Jackson include the injuries in his report. He states Officer Jackson replied saying 'It will be in the report'. Lt McCarthy state he and the EMT's thought it was unreasonable for Officer Jackson to not assist them by riding in the rear of the ambulance. While commander of the TD Garden Detail, PO Kamisha Green 135897 was out of uniform, failed to go to her post when directed to by Captain Gaughan, was disrespectful to Captain Gaughan by arguing with him, raising her voice to him and walking away from him while he was addressing these issues with her. ¶ On 3/28/2023, I was performing a paid detail as the Commander of the TD Garden Detail.  A copy of the A-1 Detail Assignment sheet  claerly states ¶ "Per Captain- All Personnel assigned to the Garden Event shall have their Traffic Vest/Mic Extension along with proper outer..." ¶ On this particular evening, PO Kamisha Green and Officer Domenic Dimarzo were assigned " Section 4" before the game, "Section 4" During the game and "Remain inside until empty and then Causeway TDG Garage after the game. ¶ When Officers Green and Dimarzo exited the building to presumably assist with traffic exiting the garage, I noticed both Officer heading to their vehicle on Haverhill St.  Neither Officer had on a yellow reflective vest, nor did Officer Green have on a uniform hat.  I directed both officers to assist with traffic and I informed both of them that it was their responsibility to have their yellow reflective vest and hat during the detail.  Officer Dimarzo proceeded to take up a post. ¶ Officer Green began yelling that she was cold and was going to her car.  It should be noted that it was not a particularly cold evening.  She again started to her car in direct insubordination to Captain Gaughan's directive.  At this time I informed her that if she abandoned her post, I would put her up on charges.  She then returned to the middle of the street where I was standing and started to debate the issue with me, so much so that Officer Dimarzio tried to step in and intervene.  I instructed him to go back and direct traffic.  I informed Officer Green that she was being very rude and disrespectful and I instructed her to make out a form 26 addressing her disrespectful behavior and have it on my desk the next day.  I asked her if she was working the next day to which she replied NO, so I instructed her to go to District 1, once relieved from the detail with the rest of the officers, and make out the Form 26 and email it to me.  She began to go on a tirade, demanding to know where my desk was so that she could comply.  I had to tell her several times to email it to me.  When I relieved the detail, she chased me down Haverhill St demanding to know where my desk was.  I informed her that I was the director of Licensing at HQ, but that I expected the Form 26 emailed to me. ¶ Apparently when she went to District 1, she encountered Sgt Paul Downey, and apparently told him of the situation.  Sgt Downey called me while I was on my way home and hoped to discuss the situation and bring it to an amicable solution.  I informed Sgt Downey that in 37 years on this job, I had only written one 1920 on a cadet, and that Officer Green's actions were so egregious that she would be the first Officer.  He stated to me that she told him the "she had fucked up" and that she normally leaves her vest inside the guest services office. He stated that Officer Green was a church going individual who was a good person and worthy of a break.  I asked Sgt Downey if after knowing me for some 30 years, he felt Officer Green actions were worth going to bat for her.  He told me she had had a bad day and that she was sorry and was worth it.  I said to Sgt Downey it would mean something if she expressed remorse for her disrespectful behavior.  He stated she would send an email or call me to which I declined.  I said it would be appropriate the next time I saw her for her to come over and say she made a mistake and to apologize.  Sgt Downey guaranteed me that that would be the first thing that Officer Green did the next time our paths crossed. ¶ Coincidentally, I again was the commander of the detail on Thursday, March 30.  Again, by some unknown coincidence, Officers Green and Dimarzo were assigned the exact details as the prior date.  As the commander of the detail, I exercised my right of assignment and Put two other officers in Section 4 before and during the game and Remain inside after the game. narrative_x: On this day, I was assigned as the Y906 Supervisor of Cases in Roxbury Court.  ADA Mauve Healey came to my office to inquire whether Officer Jairo Polanco (C-11) signed into court.  She was expecting him to appear and testify (summons attached).  I told her that I would try to contact him and get back to her.  After confirming that the summons was emailed to Officer Polanco, I contacted the district where he works (C-11). ¶ I called District C-11 x4330, identified myself and asked the male who picked up the phone if he could get me a phone number to reach Officer Polanco because he was needed for court.  He told me that he would call Officer Polanco and tell him to call me at x4378.  I don’t know who picked up the phone, but it should be on a recorded phone line.  After some time, ADA Healey returned to my office and I realized that I had not yet heard back from Officer Polanco.  This time, I called the Duty Supervisor’s line at C-11 and asked for Officer Polanco’s phone number.  When I got the phone number, I called Officer Polanco and left a voicemail telling him to call me back ASAP, that he was summoned to court.  A male called on my phone line, that appeared to be the same number I contacted.  But, when I picked up and asked if he was Officer Polanco, he said, “No, I don’t know what you’re talking about.”  I asked him if he’s saying I dialed the wrong phone number, and he said “yes.”  We hung up the phone. ¶ I called District C-11 again and spoke with Officer Jade Cheek, who confirmed the phone number for Officer Polanco that I called earlier, as initially provided by the supervisor.  She stated that they had to call Officer Polanco four times, and they finally just spoke to him.  Surprisingly, she said that he was waiting for my phone call, which implies that he still had no idea that he should be calling me back in the police room.  I followed up with an email and a text message as written documentation that the ADA was looking for him in court and that he needs to call me back. ¶ Officer Polanco called me back in the police room and identified that he was indeed Officer Polanco.  When I spoke to him, his voice sounded just like the same voice who previously said I was calling the wrong number.  I asked him if he was working right now, because I heard street noise in the background of the call.  I wanted to gauge if he was available to come to court.  He glossed right over whether he was currently working, and he told me that he believed he was the wrong witness summoned to court for the incident.  He stated that there is another Jairo Polanco who works at District B-2. ¶ I asked Officer Polanco if he notified anyone at court that he believed they summoned the wrong Jairo Polanco to court, and that the summons was meant for an officer of the same name at B-2.  He stated that he did not, but that he forwarded the email summons to the other Jairo Polanco who works at District B-2.  I asked him if he can forward me that email that he sent to the other Jairo Polanco.  I was curious whether the other Jairo Polanco actually knew about the summons.  When I asked him to forward me the summons he sent to the other Jairo Polanco, he hung up the phone on me. ¶ Officer Polanco was summoned to court, he did not appear, and when he was finally contacted, he was disrespectful regarding those inquiries about the missed court appearance.  I call officers on a daily basis about being needed for court, but this incident stands out as highly unusual.  ADA Healey stated that she had to continue the case, because Officer Polanco did not appear. ¶ I read the report narrative related to the court case. This will be a 1920 for disrespectful treatment (to a superior officer), untruthfulness (summons meant for another Polanco), and a failure to appear for court (neglect of duty). narrative_x: About 2:40pm on Monday 4/17/23, Rassol Gasson 2/8/87, age 36, of 17 Harvard Ave #1 in Dorchester MA 02121, came into District B3 to report what he felt was a negative police interaction that occurred on Thursday 4/13/23 at about 7pm. ¶ He stated that he was pulled over in his 2005 Gold Honda Odyssey (MA reg: 8GZ732) on Rosedale Street on B3.  He stated that two officers (whom he described as both being white males) approached him at the car stop and told him that his vehicle was reported as stolen.  They asked him who owned the car and if he knew, and they asked him "where did you buy it?" ¶ He gave them his license and stated that he owned the car.  And then they asked him out of the car at which time they handcuffed him and walked him back to the police car.  One of the officers then searched his vehicle while the other officer was querying the information..  At one point the officers apologized and appeared to recognize that Mr Gasson was in fact the lawful owner. ¶ Upon speaking with Mr Gasson at B3, he and I spoke for well over 30 minutes.  I queried his vehicle myself and I confirmed that (at this time) there is no "stolen" status on his car.  This had been a fear of his; that the car would be pulled over for this again.  He seems to understand that the officer's may have had a legitimate mistake in the vehicle query. narrative_x: Officer Adilson Rosa submitted a Detail Authorization Record (“detail card”) that falsely indicated National Grid did not show up on August 24, 2020, at 653 Bennington St, East Boston. narrative_x: On June 1, 2023, I spoke with Colleen Alvarez who is an investigator from the Medical Examiner's Office.  She stated the ME's Office tried for several months to have Detective Sean Deery reply to them regarding an unclaimed person from a sudden death.  On May 31, 2023, an email was sent to District 1 detective supervisors and Detective Deery sent an email that she found disrespectful and unnecessary.  She stated this has been on-going issue with Detective Deery for 2 months with the ME's Office attempting to reach Detective Derry in order to be able to bury the unclaimed person from the sudden death.  Sergeant Detective Cellucci spoke with Colleen Alvarez, and she forwarded a copy of emails, an exhaustion letter and the emails sent to Detective Derry, as well as she has documentation of phone calls made to him that were not answered.  She stated she felt his response was an attack on the ME's Office, unprofessional, disrespectful and are now included in work product related to the unclaimed person.

narrative_x: At 1627 hours on January 8, 2023 Officer Barnes received a call at 411 Washington Street for a larceny report.  The 911 Call came in at 1423 hours and was held for approximately 90  minutes.  The call was coded as a priority 7 call. ¶ Officer Barnes responded to the 90 minute old, priority 7 call with his emergency lights activated and proceeded to drive through two red lights without stopping or slowing down.  At roll call, 20 minutes prior to this call Barnes received training in rule 302. ¶ Barnes disregarded the training he received in the police academy and the roll call training he received immediately before going to this call.  Barnes put the public and himself in harm's way with his unsafe driving in addition to creating liability for the department. ¶ PO Barnes violated rule 302 sec. 4.1 (Emergency Driving) ¶ Refer to Sergeant Crossen and Lieutenant Walsh's Form 26's as well as the preserved FLIR Video in Sergeant Crossen's possession. ¶ It should be noted that On March 23, 2023 Officer Barnes was found at fault for rear ending a motor vehicle (I232022447). ¶ On February 2, 2023 Officer Barnes violated rules 309 sec. 4 (Evidence and Found Property) and rule 102 sec. 4 (Neglect of Duty) when he discarded evidence/personal property in the dumpster.  Additionally, he failed to document it in his incident report.  Again, Officer Barnes opened himself and the department up to liability. ¶ Refer to Lieutenant Walsh's Form 26. ¶ On February 8, 2023 Officer Barnes violated rule 309 sec. 4 (Evidence and Found Property) when he again discarded evidence in the dumpster. ¶ Refer to Lieutenant Walsh's Form 26. ¶ On February 12, 2023 Officer Barnes violated rule 102 sec 4 (Neglect of Duty/Judgement) when he delayed and was hesitant putting out a broadcast to fellow officers pertaining to a BOLO for a person with a gun. I was assigned as the Duty Supervisor for the First Half shift at E-18 when a broadcast was made by E-13 Officer Paul McGarty. He stated he had been threatened by a black male with a gun who fled in a motor vehicle in the area of Cummins Highway and American Legion Hwy. Officer McGarty then provided a description of the suspect and the vehicle. Multiple E18 units responded along with Patrol Supervisor Sgt Ricky Cooks. Officers briefly handcuffed and detained, Mr. Arnold Bernier of 603 Irving Road in Randolph, Mass. Officers frisked Mr. Bernier and his vehicle for a firearm with negative results. Officer McGarty did broadcast he had not seen a weapon but stated the suspect had threatened to shoot him. Sgt Cooks interviewed Mr. Bernier who stated Officer McGarty cut off his vehicle three separate times in traffic. Officer McGarty stated at a red light on Cummins Highway Mr. Bernier got out of his car and came to his window and threatened him, saying "if you cut someone off, you will be met with a gun in your face" and then made a shooting gesture with his hand. Mr Bernier stated he only shouted out the window to the officer that "That was an asshole move." It should be noted Mr. Bernier had parked in the parking lot and went to a Citizens bank while holding his 2 year old daughter when he was met by officers. Sgt Cooks after investigating the incident directed Officer Leix Alleyne assigned to the L411F car to complete an Investigate Persons incident report #232071669. Mr. Bernier and Officer McGarty were both released from the scene. Sgt Cooks Identified himself to Arnold Bernier and explained the complaint process to him. W ¶ Sgt Cooks returned to the station and made a verbal report to me. I requested Sgt Fenton search for any videos on the department system of the incident. She found video on Camera 315 located at the intersection of Cummins Highway and Hyde Park Ave on the Security Desk System. The video shows from 05:00:37 to 05:01:36 the two vehicles stopped at the red light. Traffic starts up and the two vehicles stay stationary, and it appears the two drivers are shouting at each other. The two cars then start to move and it appears Officer McGarty gives Mr. Bernier the finger as his car passes by. narrative_x: I respectfully report to you, an interaction that occurred on October 26th, 2023 with Officer Erik Shears, where his demeanor was unprofessional, disrespectful, and insubordinate. At approximately 8:00 PM I called Officer Shears to order him for a 4PM shift. I informed Officer Shears that I would have to order him for a shift tomorrow to which he replied, “back to back?” I said “yes sir, unfortunately we have to do that”. Officer Shears went on to question how he could be ordered as the detail room said he was “all set”. I informed Officer Shears  that overtime trumps details and that he would need to kick in his detail. Officer Shears replied that he had something to do with his daughter and that he was told he was all set. I once again informed Officer Shears that he was ordered and that overtime takes precedence over details. Officer Shears again questioned me saying “yeah, not back to back, you can’t do that?” At this point with four others to be ordered, I told Officer Shears that if he needed explanation on how the to-be-ordered list works, he could come to the DS office and I would explain it to him. Officer Shears quickly said he would be in and I asked how long he would be, Officer Shears replied, “five minutes”. ¶ I felt that Officer Sears was confrontational on the telephone so in anticipation he might continue on this path, I proactively contacted Officer Canto, the on duty BPPA union rep, and informed him that Officer Shears had an issue with being ordered and requested Officer Canto to assist and witness this effort. ¶ Approximately 15 minutes later Officer Shears arrived at the A-1 DS office. Officer Shears entered the office and asked what was going on. I rolled my chair over the desk closest to the office door and remained seated, and placed the to be ordered list on the desk. I began by saying the list is done by hours and his name was next. Shears questioned why there were so many people in the office for this. I replied that Officer Canto was a union rep and that it was his job to explain the list if needed, and also that Sergeant Detective Cellucci and Sergeant Plunket, who were previously in the DS office, could witness the conversation, if needed. Shears took an aggressive stance and stated in a confrontational tone, “you’ve had a problem with me since before you had stripes from that thing out there” (see summary of incident below). I replied that I had no issue and that ordering was done from a to-be-ordered list and once again tried to explain the list to him. Shears raised his voice and said, “no, you've held a grudge against me since then”. I disagreed and stated I held no grudge and asked if he could cite one example of a situation to verify that accusation. Shears quickly changed the subject and said, “I was told I was all set, I have the messages”. I replied, once again, details have nothing to do with getting ordered, there is a list. Shears interrupted me, once again raising his voice, stating that “he had texts from the detail room” and reached for his telephone. I informed him that a police officer may have told him that he was all set, but I was a Sergeant and I was informing him that he was next on the list and was ordered. Shears continued that he has no issues with anyone and that I was holding a grudge. At this time Sergeant Detective Cellucci stated to Shears “You’re aware he’s a Sergeant”?, Shears answered, Yes. “You understand you’re ordered”?, Shears answered, Yes. Sergeant Detective Cellucci then told Shears to leave the Office. ¶ During this conversation, Officer Canto attempted to slow Shears’ responses seemingly so that he would respect the rank and understand the message I was attempting to relay. Shears seemed “locked on to” me and persistent to continue with his insubordinate attitude. On July 20, 2022, the Boston Police Anti-Corruption Division received a complaint regarding a Phoenix Communications paid detail at the intersection of Cambridge and Bowdoin Street on Area A-1. The detail was scheduled from May 16, 2022 2000 hours until 0400 on May 17, 2022. The assigned officers were Sergeant Detective Carl Blando, Office of Homeland Security and Sergeant Detective Daniel Pusey of the Audit and Review Division . Blando was assigned the Phoenix Communications detail (Tracking #2547918) by the Paid Detail Assignment office at 1517 hours on May 16, 2022. ¶ Investigation: ¶ The investigation included a review of the submitted complaint - a seven-page BPD Form 26 from BPD Superintendent Marcus Eddings and a flash drive containing BTD camera footage. This was followed by an ACD interview of Sgt. Det. Carl Blando. The flash drive included footage from several different cameras in the City of Boston's traffic monitoring system. ¶ The camera located at Cambridge and Bowdoin Street revealed that Sgt. Det. Carl Blando arrived to the detail at 19:55.  Sgt. Det. Daniel Pusey arrived at the detail location at 20:03:43.  Sgt. Det. Pusey remains on-scene for a few minutes and then joins a different Phoenix Communications crew at another location which is working in concert with the Cambridge and Bowdoin site. Blando remains at Cambridge and Bowdoin for the entirety of the detail. ¶ Video showed Sgt. Det. Blando remain at the intersection of Cambridge and Bowdoin Street until his detail card is signed by Phoenix Communications supervisor, Michael Jenson. Blando drives away from the site at 00:01:01. The traffic cameras reveal that Blando performed the Phoenix Communications detail for a total of 4:06. Sgt. Det. Daniel Blando submitted and received payment for a detail card for 5 "actual hours worked." The submitted hours worked were from 2000 on May 16, 2022 to 0100 on May 17, 2022. ¶ Interview: ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando was asked if he could specifically recall a Phoenix Communications detail he performed on May 16, 2022 at Cambridge and Bowdoin Street. He stated he could not, Blando quickly added that he completes an average of five to six details per week. When informed that he worked the detail with Sgt. Det. Daniel Pusey he stated that it sounded a little familiar but that he had performed "six to eight" details with Pusey over the past year. He then pointed out that this detail was about nine months ago and it was difficult for him to remember specific facts.  He then added that he works the day shift and when he has a detail that starts at seven or eight in the evening he usually arrives early. He explained that he lives far from the City of Boston so he usually waits at work and then arrives early to his detail assignment. This is evidenced on the BTD traffic camera covering Bowdoin and Cambridge Street. I informed Blando that video showed him arrive to the detail on May 16, 2022 at 7:55 p.m. and depart at 12:01 a.m. on May 17, 2022. Blando and his attorney (Dunlap) reviewed screenshots taken from the traffic video of his arrival and departure. ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando reviewed the copy of his detail card for the job in question and answered that all of the writing appeared to be his. He stated that when a detail ends early he usually rounds the end time off "in fifteen-minute increments." He explained that he could not recall if the Phoenix Communications supervisor directed him to write in the 1:00 a.m. end time. However, he added that he knew that he had worked in excess of four hours "so he didn't see it as a difficulty because you're getting paid for eight hours regardless." ¶ Sgt. Det Blando stated that after his last detail related interview with ACD on June 30, 2022 he began keeping notes on the back of the pink copy of his detail card. The detail card, officially known as the Detail Authorization Record, comes in triplicate. The top yellow copy goes to the Paid Details Payment Unit, the middle pink copy is the officer's copy, and the bottom white copy is the customer copy. Blando described his personal note-taking process. He stated that he keeps notes on when he leaves the jobsite to use get dinner or if the crew changes their location. The Phoenix Communication crew did not leave the Cambridge and Bowdoin Street location to perform any work. They briefly relocated to A and Iron Street, South Boston (as shown by BTD video) but the crew does not set up or work. The Phoenix Communications workers merely pull to the side of the road and park for approximately a half hour while a different crew finished their work for the night. ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando stated that since performing this detail he became aware of a memorandum or email put out by Superintendent Marcus Eddings authorizing minute for minute pay on paid details. According to Blando he now puts minute by minute times on his detail cards. ¶ ACD 1 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings conducted an audit on a paid detail performed on 1/21/21, by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando. Superintendent Eddings states that Phoenix Communication worked from 19:07 hrs. to 21:10, for a total of 2 hours and 3 minutes. Superintendent Eddings said that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card 19:00 to 23:15. Indicating he worked 4hrs and 15 minutes. ¶ ACD 2 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando and Det. Nina Jefferson, on April 13,2022, at the intersection of Arch Street and Milk Street. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with a start time before his arrival. and an end time later than his departure. ¶ ACD 3 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a PV Barone paid detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando, and Officer Nicholas Beliveau on May 5, 2022.  Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with inaccurate start and end times. ¶ ACD 4 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a Feeney Brothers detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando on May 10, 2022. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with an inaccurate start and end time. ¶ ACD 5 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited l Feeney Brothers detail performed at 1200 Tremont Street by Sgt. det. Carl Blando. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with an inaccurate start and end time 5/20/22 ¶ ACD 6 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando on June 7, 2022.  Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with an inaccurate end time. ¶ As stated in Boston Police Department Special Order 04-023 - Increase in Paid Detail Rates issued on August 3, 2004: ¶ With respect to outside construction details only, time worked beyond four hours up to the eighth hour shall be paid as eight hours. Time worked in excess of eight hours shall be paid at the straight hourly detail rate. ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando worked the Phoenix Communications detail in excess of 4 hours securing his right to receive payment for 8 hours. ¶ Though problematic that Sgt. Det. Blando rounded up to the hour instead of in a 15-minute increment, I find no violation of Massachusetts General Laws and no reason to investigate this matter any further.

narrative_x: Based on a tip, ACD investigators conducted surveillance of Officer Shawn Marando from February 10 to February 24, 2024.  Marando partnered with Recruit Officer Feliz Penalo in the G101A each night.  Investigators observed the officers to be very proactive.  They regularly conducted traffic stops, enforced parking ordinances, and volunteered to take pending calls.  They regularly took Code 19s near the bars at closing time and conversed with citizens, merchants, and security personnel from the various licensed premises.  Investigators found no evidence to support the allegations in the tip. ¶ However, analyzing the G101A’s activity revealed several problematic matters.  This is especially true when RO Feliz Penalo’s probationary status is considered. ¶ There were several incidents where the officers did not properly document their interactions with motorists and other citizens, did not notify citizens they were being recorded, and did not dock their body cameras in a timely manner. narrative_x: On April 20, 2022, Sgt. Det. Marc Sullivan, Human Trafficking Unit (HTU), contacted Lt. Det. Sean Martin at ACD to notify him of the following.  Sexual Assault/HTU victim (I# 222026153) alleged that Police Officer Joshua Delisle tipped off rape suspect Albert Boynton about being wanted by the police.  (I# 222026153) also alleged that Delisle sold crack cocaine and rented hotel rooms for sexual encounters with women who frequented the Southampton St / Topeka Street area.  Lastly, (I# 222026153) alleged that Delisle offered her money in exchange for sex. ¶ An investigation was conducted at the Anti-Corruption Division, which uncovered no credible evidence supporting the allegations. ¶ However, the investigation did find evidence of potential administrative violations of Department rules and procedures.  Specifically, ¶ Rule 102 Sec. 39, Association with Criminals; ¶ Rule 102 Sec. 4, Neglect of Duty/Unreasonable Judgement for 1) transporting (I# 222026153) in POV and 2) failure to notify Operations with location, destination, and mileage; and ¶ Rule 204 Sec. 4, Failure to notify proper Duty Supervisor (D4) and Patrol Supervisors (C6 & E13) about sexual assaults.

Carnell stated that while in the academy basement hallway prior to the start of the training day, Feliciano referred to her family members as having a reputation of being racist, and asked how other recruits felt “being in a class with somebody who was entitled and racist.” Carnell further stated during Constitutional Law class, Feliciano again singled her by motioning in her direction while referencing "entitled" people. Finally, she stated that Feliciano stated in front of the entire recruit class that if anyone "wants to take me to IAD, I don’t care I’ll walk you down there myself.”

narrative_x: I was on my way home after picking up my daughter from work. I made a right turn onto Neponset Ave from Truman Hwy like I always have. As i approached the intersection of Neponset Ave & Loring street - i stopped. I looked to my left and saw a man standing at the corner with his dog (50 Neponset Ave). The man was facing my direction but his dog was facing the opposite direction and seemed to be smelling the fence. I assumed the dog was looking to release himself (use the bathroom, etc). I looked to the right of Loring Street then I looked to the left of Loring street - no cars so I proceeded through the intersection to my house. Someone was parked in front of my house so I parked in front of the house next to my house (62 Neponset Ave). As I opened my car door - I can hear a man yelling from my rear. “You didn’t even stop at the stop sign”. At first I didn’t pay him any mind as it’s 10 o’clock at night, I’m a female, I’m with my daughter and I don’t have no problem or issues with anyone on this street. I just knew whomever that was - they were not talking to me. After getting out the car, closing the door and walking to the front of my vehicle to proceed to my house - I hear the voice getting closer to me. “Ma’am - I’m talking to you!” At this point - I am now on my steps. I turn and now that same man that was at the corner with his dog is standing on the side walk next to my car. “Sir - what is your problem” I said. He then said “You didn’t stop at the stop sign - I have kids that live here - what if my kids were out.” I then said to him “Sir, I did stop at the stop sign - you didn’t look like you were going to cross and there were no cars. I live here - and been living here for 10 years - I can’t leave my house without stopping at the stop sign going down or going up. It’s automatic.” As I said I live here and been living here for 10 years - he yells “yeah right”. Then I said “If you have any issues you can come knock on this door”. Then he told me “You need to grow up!” I then looked to him as I proceeded to walk up the steps on my porch “You need to grow up! You are the one that chased me, a female, at night with your dog as I am trying to go home!” I then walk to my door to open it with the key and I said “Sir you have yourself a good night.” At that point he mumbled “You should get a ticket”. As I opened my house door - my other daughter was opening the door from the inside as she could hear me yelling from inside of the house. I turned to the man and I said “Sir, do whatever you like - write it down, take a picture, i don’t care” and then I walked into my house my daughter after me and then close the door. In April - I received a letter from the Registry of Motor Vehicles that my license was due for suspension for non-payment of a citation. I was extremely confused as I have not been pulled over in a ¶ while and I would remember being pulled over and receiving a citation. After calling the Registry and doing some research - as I thought my son or boyfriend got pulled over in my car. I found out that an electronic ticket was submitted for me failing to stop at a stop sign at the intersection of Loring & Neponset Ave. As soon as I heard the street names - I was immediately reminded of this incident with a man that was harassing me late at night coming home with my daughter. This man that walked/ran an estimate of 300ft to proceed to argue with me - never once introduced himself, nor did he tell me his was a police officer. To be honest I thought he was a crazy person and I was nervous which is why I kept my distance and stayed on my porch when speaking to him. I believe I received this ticket from Officer Jonathan (ID# 157684) because to him it was personal. He racially profiled me at the beginning with automatically thinking I didn’t live in his neighborhood and also assuming by his comment that, I myself didn’t have kids that live here. When I told him I lived at my residence for 10yr

At Approx. 02:30 AM on July 14th 2024, Sgt. MacDonald along with myself (Sgt. Gomes) were requested to speak with two parties in the District B-3 lobby, located at 1165 Blue Hill Ave. ¶ Mr. Juan Ayala-Powell (DOB: 07/13/1989) along with Ms. Leyla Pizarro (DOB: 12/25/1991) had arrived at District B-3 to speak with Supervisors in regard to a recent interaction with Boston Police Officers on a Traffic Stop in the area of 200 Harvard St., Boston MA. Mr. Ayala Powell stated to Sgt. MacDonald that they were pulled over by Boston Police Officers for no reason, pulled out of their vehicle, and assaulted. Mr. Ayala-Powell stated that he wanted the names of the Boston Police Officers involved in the incident, as well as their badge numbers. Ms. Pizarro then requested to be evaluated by EMS. Boston EMS was then requested to respond to District B-3. Ms. Pizarro was transported to the Carney Hospital for the abrasions to her knees. ¶ While Sgt. MacDonald was reviewing Body Worn Camera footage of the incident. I (Sgt. Gomes) had gone to speak with Mr. Ayala-Powell in regards to the incident. Sgt. MacDonald returned a short time later, also to again speak with Mr. Ayala-Powell. During this time of Mr. Ayala-Powell giving his narrative, Sgt. MacDonald informed him of several discrepancies regarding his accounts from the incident compared to Body Worn Camera footage. Sgt. MacDonald provided Mr. Ayala-Powell the Incident #, all of the Officers Names/Badge Numbers, as well as how to make a record request for Body Worn Camera footage. Mr. Ayala-Powell then informed me and Sgt. Macdonald " I have everything I need; I really appreciate your help."  I then provided Mr. Ayala-Powell my department card, badge number, as well as my contact information. Mr. Ayala-Powell then left District B-3. ¶ Following the conversation at District B-3, I proceeded to the Carney Hospital to speak with Ms. Pizarro in regard to this incident. I (Sgt. Gomes) then photographed Ms. Pizarro's physical injuries. I then spoke to the medical staff at the Carney Hospital as well. I provided Ms. Pizarro with my department card, badge number, as well as my contact information. ¶ Due to the Initial statements made by both Mr. Ayala-Powell, Ms. Pizarro, as well as speaking to the Officers involved in this incident, I, (Sgt. Gomes) am making this notification into the Blue Notes system. I, (Sgt. Gomes) will conduct a Use of Force investigation into this incident and will be further investigated.

narrative_x: Background: On 7/1//24 at about 11:45pm, units from B3 were dispatched to 231 Talbot Ave for a disturbance.  Onscene, they encountered a large crowd that flagged them down and pointed out a vehicle that they stated had just struck someone and was operating recklessly.  They observed the vehicle come back around an drive back in toward the crowd and directly at another person.  No other people were struck.  The officers (with onscene help from some State Police that observed this going on),  were able to surround the vehicle and the operator (Manuel Rodrigues 9/17/2003).  The arrest was made after a State Trooper broke the window to access and apprehend the operator with the B3 units. ¶ The operator (Rodrigues) was arrested and asked the officers to please not tow his car. ¶ A male approached the officers and stated that he was the brother of the arrested operator.  He asked if he could take the car.  The officers asked if he had a license and he stated that he only had a permit; however, he was with a fried who had an active license.  That friend (Dellon Giles 6/22/2006) was queried, and it was confirmed that he had an active license.  They were then given the keys to the car. ¶ Back at the booking area, the officers advised Rodrigues that they had spared him the tow and given the car keys to his brother.  Rodrigues stated that he did not have a brother.  The officers showed him a picture of Giles and Rodrigues stated that he did not know him.  The officers were unclear if he was being dishonest, messing with them, or telling the truth.  Nonetheless, they sought out to look for the vehicle.  Another unit located the car about 2 blocks away from Giles' home address (near Ripley and Vassar).  There was apparent damage to the vehicle.  It was then towed for safe keeping. ¶ After confirming that Rodrigues remained steadfast that he did not know Dellon Gilles, the officers submitted a criminal complaint against Dellon Giles for stealing the car by falsely portraying himself as a family member to the police. ¶ Complaint: ¶ About 2:45am on 7/17/24, Manuel Rodrigues came into B3 to complain about the experience. narrative_x: Thursday July 10, 2024, I was informed by Detective Janet Lewis #099731that she was involved in an off-duty accident in the town of Walpole.  Detective Lewis stated the accident happened on July 8, 2024, around 1930 hours at the intersection of Route 1 and Coney St.   She stated the accident was a minor fender bender and after the accident she attempted to pull into a safer location to exchange paperwork. She attempted to exchange paperwork, but the male was belligerent and yelling at her about her trying to take off. Detective Lewis stated she asked him if he had her plate information to what she believed he stated he did.  At that moment Detective Lewis left the scene. I then informed Detective Lewis to write a Form 26 of the events that transpired and forward the report to me.

narrative_x: On Saturday, March 2, 2024, at approximately 17:17 hours, Officer Shoulla was conducting a code 19 at Alo (149 Newbury Street). While conducting the code 19, Officer Shoulla spoke with store manager, Marissa Simone. Ms. Simone informed Officer Shoulla that a past known shoplifter, later identified as the suspect, Timothy Talbot, was currently in the dressing room with assorted merchandise.  Officer Shoulla immediately called for additional units to assist him. ¶ While waiting for backup, Officer Shoulla stood outside of the store at 149 Newbury Street to make sure he was able to observe the suspect in the store and be able to stop him if he attempted to exit.  Officer Shoulla observed suspect Talbot conceal an item on his person and exit the store.  As the suspect exited the store and prior to assistance arriving, Officer Shoulla stopped Talbot and advised him he was being stopped for shoplifting.  Officer Shoulla gave the suspect a verbal command to put his hands behind his back in order to be handcuffed.  Talbot actively resisted Officer Shoulla's attempt at gaining control and attempted to break away from his hold.  Officer Shoulla repeatedly informed Talbot that if he did not stop resisting, he would be sprayed with OC spray.  The suspect continued to actively resist which in Officer Shoulla deploying his department issued OC spray in the direction of the suspect to gain control.  After being sprayed in the eyes, Talbot was still able to break away from Officer Shoulla's hold and flee on foot without his jacket or shirt on.  Talbot was then located and arrested behind 28 Exeter Street after a foot chase.  Multiple other units, as well as walking beat supervisor, Lieutenant Pusey, responded to the scene.  Officer Shoulla informed Lieutenant Pusey that he failed to activate his body worn camera during rush to control and arrest the suspect. ¶ Officers requested EMS and Boston EMS (A93) arrived on scene to treat suspect Talbot for OC exposure before officers transported him to D-4 for booking. It was later revealed that the suspect had concealed on his person, 2 pairs of shorts and 5 pairs of pants from Alo, totaling $776.00 in value.

narrative_x: On July 10, 2021, Officer Randall Martin, ID# 131276, was assigned to the J201A in District E-13.  At approximately 4:30 a.m., he and other officers responded to a call for a person shot at 360-B Centre St, JP.  On arrival, Martin observed ballistic evidence and a blood trail leading from the front door of the building.  The shooting victim, Kevin Desruisseaux, was located by another officer a few blocks away. ¶ Martin knew this location housed an illegal after-hours nightclub owned and operated by his good friend and Academy classmate, Boston Police Officer McDermott, and Boston Public Health Commission (BPHC) Police Officer Luigi D’Addieco. ¶ While on the scene, Martin received text messages from McDermott, who was inside 360-B Centre St, refusing to open the door for the police. ¶ Martin also sent and received texts from D’Addieco, who was watching investigating officers from his vehicle parked across the street. ¶ Martin also knew Desruisseaux was a doorman at the club. ¶ Investigating officers heard voices coming from inside the building and needed to enter.  They did not know whether any suspects were inside.  They did not know whether any additional victims were inside.  The Patrol Supervisor requested SWAT. ¶ Approximately an hour after officers arrived, SWAT made a forced entry into the building and located dozens of party-goers holed up in the basement nightclub, including McDermott. ¶ Although Martin possessed vital knowledge regarding the shooting and the occupied after-hours nightclub, he did not share it with anyone at the scene.  Martin kept this information to himself while his E-13 colleagues, SWAT officers, and K-9 officers investigated, devised a plan, and forced entry into the nightclub.  Moreover, Martin did not disclose any of this information afterward.  Concealing and omitting this pertinent information violates the Department's truthfulness policy. ¶ Anti-Corruption investigated the incident and interviewed Martin.  A Suffolk County Grand Jury ultimately indicted McDermott and D'Addieco. ¶ Martin testified during the grand jury proceedings. ¶ Martin testified that he could not recall the context of the communications he and McDermott had on the night of the shooting. ¶ Martin testified that he knew D'Addieco was across the street that night but could not recall the context of his and D'Addieco's communications. ¶ McDermott testified that he and McDermott had discussed the Department's investigation into the shooting. ¶ Martin testified that he had not discussed what he knew about the nightclub or that night with anyone from the Boston Police Department (other than McDermott) until Anti-Corruption investigators interviewed him. ¶ On July 10, 2021, Officer Randall Martin, ID# 131276, was assigned to the J201A in District E-13. narrative_x: On call investigator spoke to complainant Mr. Donnie Myers on the phone for forty minutes. Mr. Myers stated that he is the rightful owner of the land at 15 and 17 West Cottage Street, but that the city has attempted to take the land through eminent domain and had his lock and fence around the property cut in order to have the land surveyed on several occasions. ¶ Specifically, Myers alleged the following that Officer Marc Coleman was rude and disrespectful to him while conducting a paid detail at 11 West Cottage Street on February 7, 2025. Officer Coleman also allegedly blocked Myers from accessing his own property by stepping in front of him, did not include pertinent details in the police report I252010194), refused to identify employees of the surveying company hired by the city, and lied to the responding sergeant (Sgt. Dennis Crawley) about statements he made to Myers prior to the sergeant's arrival. ¶ Myers received a notice to appear for a magistrate hearing concerning a threats charge and alleged that Det. James O'Laughlin used this as a false allegation in an attempt to intimidate Myers on behalf of the City of Boston. ¶ Myers also received a call from Sgt. Det. Amy Devito on 2/7/25. He stated that Sgt. Det. Devito was "friendly" and took the time to listen to his concerns, but alleged that she attempted to influence him to not pursue his fight against the city over the West Cottage Street property. ¶ Myers alleged that the city of Boston neighborhood Development department has partnered with high-ranking officers inside the B2 station to prevent his claims of vandalism (lock and fence being cut) from being investigated by detectives.

narrative_x: At approximately 7:30 PM, I received a distressing call from my 24-year-old son, informing me that my 15-year-old son had been struck by a police vehicle and had suffered a broken limb. To my shock and frustration, I was not contacted by law enforcement or medical personnel—despite the fact that my son is a minor with underlying health conditions due to being in remission. ¶ My son has no prior encounters with law enforcement, yet no one has provided a clear explanation for why such excessive force was used. He was simply on his way home with friends, adhering to his 8 PM curfew. While I am grateful that he is alive, this incident could have easily ended in tragedy, particularly given his medical history. ¶ I am outraged and deeply concerned about how the police are handling situations in our community. While I understand the importance of public safety, the reckless and aggressive actions taken in this case have left my child severely injured and traumatized. As a result, he now requires surgery, I must take multiple days off work to care for him, and I need to arrange counseling to help him process this traumatic event. Additionally, I must coordinate closely with his school to ensure he does not fall behind academically, as he is in his final year of middle school and already has frequent medical appointments due to his remission. ¶ The following is my son’s firsthand account of the incident: ¶ *“My friends and I pulled into Raymond Tire because we heard a noise coming from the scooter we were riding. The scooter was stalling, and we stopped to try to fix it. Suddenly, an unmarked black vehicle with no lights or sirens approached us, and undercover officers got out. As more officers arrived, I decided to walk away. I was on the sidewalk when a marked blue-and-white police cruiser hit me and ran over my foot. After that, I blacked out. The next thing I remember was being on the sidewalk in pain, yelling for an ambulance. I immediately called my brother so he could let my mom know what had happened. ¶ As I regained awareness, I overheard a white officer instructing someone to arrest me. However, the only Black officer on the scene refused, stating that I needed medical attention for my foot. I was left in pain for an extended period before finally being transported to the hospital.”* ¶ This incident is unacceptable. My child—an unarmed minor with a serious medical history—was struck by a police vehicle, left in distress, and nearly arrested instead of immediately receiving medical attention. The fact that law enforcement failed to notify me, his parent, only adds to the negligence and disregard for his well-being. ¶ I demand answers. I demand accountability. No parent should have to experience the fear, frustration, and anger that I feel right now. I will not rest until those responsible are held accountable for their actions and meaningful changes are made to prevent this from happening to another child. narrative_x: On June 26, 2025, the on-call IAD investigator received a telephone call from Jamie Higgins regarding a car stop and her subsequent arrest on May 26, 2023. Higgins stated that she is filing the complaint now, as her court case has been dismissed, and she has gained access to the body-worn camera footage from the involved Boston Officer, Nadine Powell, and the involved Massachusetts State Trooper, Austin Rose. She also stated that she is medically disabled due to the stop and now suffers from PTSD. It should be noted that Higgins stated another Boston Police Officer was on the scene, but she did not have a complaint against this officer. ¶ Jamie Higgins stated that she was stopped by State Trooper Rose, who Boston Police Officers assisted. During this stop, Higgins said she went to look at the license plate on the Boston Police vehicle because she could not see the officers' badges due to their all-black clothing. She said while attempting to do so, she was grabbed inappropriately by Officer Powell, who attempted to put her into a "choke-hold" that was ultimately unsuccessful because Higgins was able to "slip out of it." Higgins then told Officer Powell that she could not put her hands on her, to which Powell responded that she could do what she wanted. Higgins further stated that Officer Powell told her brother on the scene, Jarrett, that she was "Going to fight your sister." Higgins said that this statement occurred within the initial silent 30 seconds of Officer Powell's body-worn camera footage. Trooper Rose ultimately arrested Higgins in a manner she described as "violent" and which she correlated to her medical disability. ¶ Jamie Higgins said that she is going through the State Police complaint procedure regarding Trooper Rose. She stated that she understood the Boston Police investigation only pertained to the actions of Boston Police officers. allegation_x: Body Worn Camera Policy - Activation & Incidents of use
narrative_x: As part of a visible injury investigation (Prisoner fell while trying to run from officers) it was discovered that neither of the two officers had their Body Worn Cameras activated as required  by Boston Police Department Rule 405. While in transport to the court house (South Boston) the prisoner,  being escorted, had attempted to run from the officers and fell. She sustained scrapes and was treated at D-4 by Boston EMS. In reviewing the available evidence and reports submitted, there were no videos for review from either officer. Officer Glaropoulos stated she had removed her outer most garment and when the call came in, had left without realizing her BWC was still on it. Officer Nolen was of the opinion, that due to the very short time of transferring the prisoner (From Glaropoulos' cruiser) to the court officers, it was not warranted to activate it. ¶ Sergeant Dickson conducted the investigation and found the circumstances and injuries occurred as reported. He also counseled the officers regarding their Body Worn Cameras. ¶ I also counseled the officers, I told Officer Glaropoulos that any time she removes the camera on her outermost garment, she should immediately place it on her new outermost garment. I told Officer Nolen that she should not consider those factors or opinions regarding the activation of her Body Worn Camera but should abide by the Boston Police Rules and Regulations. Both officers were advised to review Rule 405 regarding Body Worn Cameras and were given oral reprimands for this matter. ¶ I believe both officers are aware of their errors and they will take the steps to avoid this re-occurring. ¶ As part of a visible injury investigation (Prisoner fell while trying to run from officers) it was discovered that neither of the two officers had their Body Worn Cameras activated as required  by Boston Police Department Rule 405. He stated the incident first started when a car with tinted windows and a female driver was riding his bumper inches away while he was driving on Commonwealth Avenue near the Old Veterans Building now known as the Residences at Brighton Marine 1465 Commonwealth Ave.  He further stated that the female operator beeped her horn constantly at him until another car stopped directly in front of him. ¶ At this point, Mr. Wardsworth stated the off-duty officer who was in uniform pants, displayed a badge from around his neck, and pointed a black handgun at him. Mr. Wardsworth stated he responded saying "you isn't no cop you aren't acting like no cop". Wardsworth stated he began to argue with the officer yelling back and forth. According to the incident report, the suspect/complainant Wardsworth left the scene and was stopped by officers with body cameras on in Fidelis Way.  Boston Housing Authority located video footage of a female exiting the suspects' vehicle with a bag in her hand and enter into 31 Jette Court.  The suspect/complainant was reportedly combative with officers who were surrounded by a crowd during the verbal altercation. Selina Griffin, Assistant GM for the Ramada Hotel located at 800 Morrissey Blvd., reported that one of her employees, Shaly Almedia, stated that she had been hit in the face by her boyfriend, causing a black eye. Although Almedia did not say the boyfriend's name, Ms. Griffin said she knows Almedia's boyfriend is BPD Officer Andolphe Joseph. Ms. Griffin says she reported this to Almedia's mother, and when Officer Joseph found out, he began to call and text Ms. Griffin from Almedia's phone. He then continued to text Ms. Griffin from his personal number and eventually emailed Ms. Griffin's workplace after she blocked him. Ms. Griffin considered Officer Joseph's pattern of conduct to be harassment. ¶ An intake interview was completed with Selina Giffin. ¶ A witness interview was completed with Caroline Benhaga (Ramada Hotel employee). ¶ Emails and text messages provided by Ms. Griffin were uploaded with this complaint.

allegation_x: Authorization & Use of Less-Lethal Weapons (2 counts)
narrative_x: On Wednesday, 12/11/24 Officers were called to 39 Warren Street, Roxbury for an EDP. Upon arrival Officers made their way to the 3rd floor to apartment 321 and announced their presence to the victim (Christopher Dooley). The victim instructed officers to enter his apartment and when officers opened the door they observed the victim to be sitting in an armchair with a kitchen knife to his chest. The victim had the tip on the knife pressed to his chest. The victim was slurring his speech and stated he had consumed alcohol today. The victim stated he was suffering from depression and that his family could not talk to him. Officers remained at the doorway and spoke with the victim in an attempt to de-escalate the situation. The B-2 Best team clinician responded and attempted to speak with the victim.  The victim was confrontational towards officers and the BEST team clinician. The victim stated that officers should not come into his apartment or it would not be pretty. The victim still had the knife pressed to his chest in an attempt to harm himself. Officers continued to talk to the victim to get him to put down the knife to offer mental health assistance. After exhausting all attempts to de-escalate the victim as well as offering mental health support officers requested a less lethal shotgun to the scene. Sgt. Det. Blando deployed the less lethal shotgun and fired 3 beanbag sock rounds. Officers observed the victim be struck twice with the beanbag less lethal rounds, one in the left arm and one in the stomach area. Officers immediately made entry into the apartment and seized the knife and placed the victim into handcuffs. ¶ The Firearm Discharge Investigation Team (FDIT) determined in their final report that Sergeant Detective Blando did not announce “Beanbag” before his discharge of the weapon, nor did he designate lethal coverage as required by Rule 303A.
